title: Webapp UX smoothing pass
description:
10. Webapp UX smoothing pass** — open-ended; interview user for pain points first.
  Sub-items surfaced from handoffs: (a) inspector `«` rail button is a CSS pseudo-element,
  not keyboard-focusable; (b) text-selection drag over empty timeline background closes the
  inspector; (c) inspector drawer width cramped for conversation reading;
  (d) unattributed steps' only signal is a muted rail dot + spine break — enough, or add a
  tooltip/tag like "git baseline" / "user edit"? (`eventKind` already reaches the view-model,
  `webapp/views/timeline.js:47`; handoff-20260707-1805); (e) `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` hunk rows render
  visibly between diff hunks — hide if they read as noise? (implementation-notes-proud-gosling);
  (f) inline/side-by-side diff toggle is session-only — persist in localStorage, or per-surface
  defaults (drawer inline, full view split)? (implementation-notes-proud-gosling);
  (g) inspector snapshot-drawer 50/50 split unverified visually — `.inspector-content`
  (`webapp/styles.css:124`) may need `display: flex; flex-direction: column` for the
  `max-height: 50%` panes to split correctly; eyeball s43 line 126
  (implementation-notes-items14-23-26-33-close);
  (h) `[View in File History]` button (`webapp/inspector.js:310`) renders unstyled inside the
  JSON `<pre>` — needs dedicated CSS if it reads as plain text
  (implementation-notes-items14-23-26-33-close).
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (all sub-items, user-decided "do all of them"):** (a) premise was wrong —
  no pseudo-element existed; the real gap was collapse = `display:none` with NO reopen
  affordance (`handleInspectorRailClick` was unreachable dead code, now commented out). The
  collapse button now toggles a 24px `.collapsed` rail, same focusable button flips »/«.
  (b) `checkSelectionBlocksBackgroundClose` guards the timeline background-close against
  selection drags. (c) timeline details split 60/40 → 50/50. (d) unattributed steps get a
  `timeline-tag` + tooltip naming their event kind(s) via `computeUnattributedStepTag`
  ("user edit", "script run", …). (e) `@@` hunk rows render as thin dashed separators
  (CSS-only; view-model untouched). (f) diff toggle persists via localStorage
  (`resolveInitialDiffDisplayMode`). (g) snapshot-drawer split fixed: `.inspector-content`
  becomes a flex column when the drawer is open. (h) button styled via `.snapshot-history-btn`.
  7 new view-model tests (written, not run — user runs the suite).

title: Disk-backed sandbox memo
description:
11. Disk-backed sandbox memo** — persist sha256→outcome across server restarts; the only
  remaining lever on the 7.3s cold s84 load (38 distinct python3 runs + parse).
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (user-approved):** opt-in via `configureSandboxMemoPersistence(path)`
  (`src/reconstruction_script_execution.ts`) — only `viewer_server.ts` configures it at startup
  (`.cache/sandbox-memo.json`, already gitignored); engine CLI and tests stay memory-only so
  spawn-count tests remain deterministic. Whole-file JSON rewrite after each new spawn mirrors
  the LRU-256 cap; memoized failures round-trip as `post: null`. 3 tests in
  `tests/reconstruction_script_execution.test.ts` (written, not run — user runs the suite).

title: Viewer request-path tab in `engine-pipeline-diagrams.html`
description:
12. Viewer request-path tab in `engine-pipeline-diagrams.html`** — records/document caches
  currently get one line on the cache_lru node.
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (user-approved):** tab `5 · Viewer request path` added — 20 nodes /
  4 subgraphs covering every `/api/*` route in `handleRequest`, the consent gate, the
  `buildProjectDocument` chain, and the three caches (`parsedRecordsCache` LRU 8,
  `builtDocumentCache` LRU 8, sandbox memo LRU 256 + its new item-11 disk backing). Rendered
  headlessly to verify zero mermaid errors.

title: Cache serialized `JSON.stringify(document)`
description:
13. Cache serialized `JSON.stringify(document)`** — only if reload latency ever shows it
  (ponytail note in `src/viewer_api.ts`).
  **Closed 2026-07-08 as YAGNI:** measured on s84 (the biggest scenario): `JSON.stringify`
  of the document is 0.5ms / 69KB. The reload path's real cost is python spawns + parse
  (item 11); a serialized-string cache saves half a millisecond. Nothing built.

title: ReconstructionCorpus (Fix 2)
description:
14. ReconstructionCorpus (Fix 2) — still worth building?** — from handoff 22:32. The corpus
  facade targeted duplication that `f6d2852` has since mostly eliminated (186→38 spawns, 0.03s warm),
  and the recorded scope decision rejected document-shape changes. Decide with user whether the
  architectural consolidation is still justified or the remaining lever is just item 11.
  Check `git show f6d2852 b79cf1b` + `src/cache_lru.ts` before any design work.
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (built, user-decided):** per-build cache state consolidated into
  `src/reconstruction_corpus.ts` — `CorpusState` holds records-pure branch selections plus
  reader/exec-gate-validated derived caches (histories, lineage seeds, executions), replacing
  the five identity-keyed WeakMaps in `reconstruction_branch.ts` / `reconstruction_branches.ts`
  / `reconstruction_script_stage.ts` (old declarations commented with an item-14 marker).
  Public functions, compute pipelines, cycle guards, the content-addressed sandbox memo, and
  the viewer LRUs are unchanged; no facade/forwarding layer (handoff-2232's `historiesFor(...)`
  facade shape deliberately not built). Bonus fix: `executeRunOnce`'s memo now invalidates on
  reader-identity/exec-gate changes like its siblings (previously unchecked). +4 tests in
  `tests/reconstruction_memo.test.ts`; 6 existing memo invariants untouched.

title: Fix s85 git-repo durability
description:
15. Fix s85 git-repo durability** — `readCommittedFileContent`
  (`src/reconstruction_git_evidence.ts:86`) resolves s85's repo via the RECORDED temp cwd and
  silently returns `undefined` when it's gone; temp cleanup will regress s85 steps 4–10. Fall back
  to the preserved repo at `scenarios/executed/s85-git-commit-csv-and-move-scripts/.git`.
  (handoff-api-from-scenarios-20260702-0800, "flagged not fixed".)
  **Status 2026-07-07:** s85 FAIL 3/10 in scenario coverage. git-operations.test.ts passes 3/3
  (extraction works), but the reconstructed file content is wrong because `readCommittedFileContent`
  can't reach the temp repo.
  **Done 2026-07-07:** the predicted regression landed (macOS purged the temp repo's `.git`
  internals — dir survived, `HEAD`/refs gone — surfacing as the s85 "regression" first blamed on
  the Jul-5 engine commits; bisect showed no code change was at fault). `readCommittedFileContent`
  now takes an optional preserved-repo dir, and `placeGitCommitEvidence` derives it from the
  transcript's own directory (`getRecordSource`) when a `.git` sits next to the transcript —
  scenario captures preserve a clone there; live `~/.claude/projects` transcripts don't, so the
viewer path is untouched. Scenario coverage back to 85/85.

title: Phase B `kept[]` single-gate
description:
16. Phase B `kept[]` single-gate — finish or retire?** — `src/reconstruction_parse_lines.ts`
  header still promises "Phase B makes `kept[]` the engine's sole input"; no consumer exists and
  85/85 was reached via the old path (handoff-api-from-scenarios-20260626-1152). Either finish the
  refactor or retire the plan and fix the stale header.
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (retired, user-decided):** the finish path was empirically disproven — gating
  at load caused 5 branch-test regressions (the engine walks the last-prompt/parentUuid DAG), and
  the shipped resolution gates extraction per-record via `recordVerdict` while full records flow to
  `reconstructBranches`; 85/85 coverage was reached without kept[] as sole input. Stale header
  rewritten to describe what actually shipped. No behavior change.

title: WebApp: convert to TypeScript and add build step
description:
18. WebApp: convert to TypeScript and add build step** — all 10 webapp files are plain `.js`
  served directly by the node server with no transpilation. Add a build step (esbuild/tsc) so
  webapp source is TypeScript, output is bundled JS.
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (tsc transpile, no bundler — user-approved approach):** all 10 webapp files
  `git mv`'d to `.ts` and fully typed under strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess (zero `as any`;
  local `Wire*` types for serialized JSON shapes; `declare global` for the script-tag xterm
  globals). New `tsconfig.webapp.json` emits to `webapp/dist/` with
  `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` (source imports `.ts` like `src/`, emitted JS imports `.js`);
  `npm run build:webapp`, and `npm run app` builds first. The server serves `.js` from
  `webapp/dist/` and everything else (index.html, styles.css, vendor/) from `webapp/` via
  `resolveStaticFilePath` (`src/viewer_api.ts`, +2 tests in `tests/viewer-static.test.ts`).
  `fetchDocument`/`peekCachedDocument`/`fetchJson` are generic so each view names the wire
  fields it reads. Zero behavior changes (timeline.ts verified byte-identical after
  transpilation); zero new dependencies; vendor/ untouched. Tests written/adapted, not run —
  user runs the suite.

title: 'Jump to File History Snapshot' button
description:
19. 'Jump to File History Snapshot' button** — a per-revision button in the timeline
  (reminiscent of filter buttons from previous HTML viewer versions) that navigates to the
  file-history view anchored at that revision's snapshot.
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** each chip row with a changeId resolvable to a surviving revision gets
  a `⤷` action chip ("Jump to File History Snapshot") routing to
  `#/project/<name>/file/<path>/rev/<n>` via the new `computeSnapshotJumpRoute`
  (`webapp/views/timeline.js`); unresolvable changeIds get no button. 3 tests in
  `tests/timeline-viewmodels.test.ts`.

title: FileViewer: Diff vs Base
description:
20. FileViewer: Diff vs Base — design polish** — `webapp/views/diff-vs-base.js` exists
  (62 lines) but is self-described as "Debugging surface — plain, no polish (plan 3.7)".
  Needs a designed UI: revision selector, side-by-side vs unified toggle, proper styling.

  toggle, line-number gutters, 3 context lines — plus the revision selector with `/vsbase/<n>`

title: "Snippet: Show as formatted text"
description:
21. "Snippet: Show as formatted text"** — raw-lines view (`webapp/views/raw-lines.js`)
  shows JSONL lines as raw JSON text. Add a mode/button that renders a selected line's content
  as formatted, readable text (e.g. "line 123 of 234 lines" context label + pretty-printed or
  human-readable content instead of raw JSON).
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** the JSON inspector's nav bar gains a "Show as formatted text" toggle
  (`extractReadableText`, `webapp/inspector.js`): message text, tool_result output, and
  tool_use string inputs render with real newlines; unknown blocks become placeholders;
  records with no message content show no toggle. The nav's existing `line n / total` label
  is the context readout. Session-sticky mode; 7 tests in
  `tests/inspector-viewmodels.test.ts`.

title: Clear console when loading new session
description:
22. Clear console when loading new session** — the xterm progress console retains output
  from the previous project/session load. Clear it on new navigation.
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** `renderRoute` clears the console via `progressTerminal.clear()` when
  navigation starts loading a different project (`checkNavigationStartsNewProjectLoad`,
  `webapp/app.js`); same-project sub-route hops and the projects list keep the output; the
  projects-folder switch resets tracking. Covered by 4 tests in
  `tests/route-predicates.test.ts`.

title: `fb2558d7813b8799@v2`-style blob changeIds stay unlinked
description:
23. `fb2558d7813b8799@v2`-style blob changeIds stay unlinked**  — blobs whose prefix
  matches no changeId in the document get no xterm link. Needs a server-side blob→path map
  if linking is wanted (from `implementation-notes-implement-clickable-jsonl-lines.md`).
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** re-scoped with the user to the Details view (the JSON inspector) —
  the dead tokens were `backupFileName` values whose file's revisions carry record-UUID
  changeIds, not blob names (s43's `tests/test_inventory.py` is the live demo, line 126).
  Now every `backupFileName` in a snapshot record resolves against disk via `GET /api/blob`
  (`readBlobSnapshot` in `src/viewer_api.ts`, owner-session dir only): on-disk blobs render
  as "view snapshot" links opening a bottom drawer (JSON above, verbatim blob content below)
  plus a `[View in File History]` button anchored by `backupTime`; missing blobs get a dimmed
  "(missing from disk)" suffix. No blob→path map was needed — the snapshot record itself maps
  path → blob. Tests in `tests/viewer-api.test.ts` + `tests/inspector-viewmodels.test.ts`.

title: s39 attribution: git rows land on synthetic turn
description:
24. s39 attribution: git rows land on synthetic turn** — s39 session 1's reply text
  precedes its tool calls, so file chips + git rows land on a synthetic empty-text Step 5
  instead of the reply (Step 4). The attribution rule is user-approved; changing it needs an
  explicit user decision. (handoff-develop-20260707-1619)
  **Re-verified reproducible 2026-07-08; repro for the user:** open
  `#/project/s39-git-baseline-seed/timeline` — Step 4 shows only the reply text "Setting up
  the repo, files, and branch." with NO chips/git rows; Step 5 is an empty-text agent turn
  carrying the 2 file chips (`orders.py`, `tests/test_orders.py`) and 2 git rows. In session
  `b9783f4b-…-98dccaf26fd6.jsonl` the reply record is raw line 32; its tool calls (git init /
  Write / git add+commit) follow at lines 33-66 — same turn, but the engine splits at the
  text record. Decision still pending: keep the honest split, or merge a trailing tool-only
  agent turn's rows into the preceding reply step.
  **Closed 2026-07-09 (user-decided via item 55):** neither merge nor split-as-was — tool
  calls became standalone UN-BUBBLED rows sorted chronologically between the bubbles
  (git init / ls / rtk ls / mkdir render between Step 4's reply and Step 5's files bubble),
  and the files bubble KEEPS its own step number. Verified headlessly on s39.

title: s84 Step 17: pickable agent turn with zero visible chips
description:
25. s84 Step 17: pickable agent turn with zero visible chips** — its snapshot's changeIds
  resolve to no revision and `changedPaths` is empty. Engine data question, unaddressed.
  (handoff-develop-20260707-1619)
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (investigated):** the zero-chip pickable turn (now Step 23; step
  numbering shifted since the handoff) is the `apply_renames.py` script run rewriting
  `core_inventory.py` at 20:53:49.772Z. The step timeline and the file histories are separate
  replays, and each stamps the synthetic script-execution event with its own `randomUUID()`
  (`reconstruction_script_stage.ts:303`), so the step's changeId can never join a revision —
  documented best-effort (`reconstruction_json.ts:175-177`, `:216-218`). Verdict: known,
  documented engine data gap; the turn is real and correctly pickable. A real fix
  (deterministic synthetic changeIds shared by both replays) is a design decision — raise as
  a new item if wanted.

title: `git branch` scenario fixture missing
description:
26. `git branch` scenario fixture missing** — `GitOperationKind.branch` rendering and
  detail parsing are covered by parser design only, not by a scenario fixture. Add expectation
  to `tests/git-operations.test.ts` if/when a git-branch scenario is recorded.
  (handoff-develop-20260707-1619)
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** the regenerated s41 capture (run 20260708-105945) records
  `git checkout -b feature` in its baseline session; pinned in
  `tests/git-operations.test.ts::test_s41_two_session_git_operations_include_branch_creation`
  via the new `S41_JSONL_PATHS` fixture (sequence captured live before writing the test:
  init, add, commit "baseline", checkout "feature", add, commit "wip"). Note: branch creation
  was captured as the `checkout` subcommand, so `GitOperationKind.checkout` is what gains
  fixture coverage; `GitOperationKind.branch` shares the identical detail parser
  (`findFirstNonFlagArgument`, `src/reconstruction_git_evidence.ts:141-146`) and the literal
  `git branch` subcommand remains parser-design-only.

title: Trailing-newline artifact
description:
27. Trailing-newline artifact** — 2 files show `recon=''` one line beyond reference EOF
  in item-15 pass-per-line coverage. Worth a follow-up to confirm it's a trailing-`\n` split
  artifact vs a real reconstruction bug (`implementation-notes-item15-pass-per-line.md:167`).
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** duplicate of completed roadmap item 14. Both evidence records are
  Read tool_result dumps ending in a final numbered empty line (`…\n85\t` / `…\n498\t`) — the
  "terminal Read phantom" fixed by `dropTrailingReadPhantom` (`api/numbered-entries.js`);
  item-14 gates recorded both files going mismatched 1→0
  (`plans/implementation-notes-item14-trailing-extent.md:64-65`). The
  `tools/line-state-reports/*.json` reports are stale pre-fix outputs (2026-06-11), and the
  follow-up note actually lives at `implementation-notes-per-line-state-sidecar-plan.md:166`,
  predating the fix. The live engine is unaffected (its `splitLines` drops the trailing empty
  element). No code change.

title: 362 golden-value test failures
description:
28. 362 golden-value test failures** — retired in favor of the scenario coverage tool
  (85/85 scenarios fully reproduced as of 2026-07-08; zero references to golden-value tests
  remain in the test suite).

title: Rename the "Jump to conversation" button
description:
29. Rename the "Jump to conversation" button** — it now jumps to the timeline anchored
  at the step + transcript inspector, not the conversation view. "Jump to timeline" /
  "Jump to step"? One-string change once the user picks a label. (handoffs 1632/1805)
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** renamed to "Jump to timeline step" (user-picked label),
  `webapp/views/file-history.js`.

title: Simplify `openRevision` in `webapp/inspector.js` (~226)
description:
30. Simplify `openRevision` in `webapp/inspector.js` (~226)** — its
  `!checkRouteIsTimeline(...)` branch is dead on all project routes, and it swaps drawer
  content WITHOUT updating the URL — inconsistent with the URLs-reflect-drawers architecture.
  Replacing it with `location.hash = routeToFileHistory(...) (+ /rev/N)` deletes the branch
  and makes revision links shareable, at the cost of a full timeline re-render per click.
  (handoff 1632)
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** `openRevision` is now a hash navigation via the new
  `computeRevisionLinkRoute` (`webapp/inspector.js`); the dead `!checkRouteIsTimeline` branch
  and the direct drawer render are gone, revision links are shareable URLs. 2 tests in
  `tests/inspector-viewmodels.test.ts`.

title: Remove the dead "(unattributed)" CSS hide rule
description:
31. Remove the dead "(unattributed)" CSS hide rule** — `6b5a71a` hid the lane header
  via CSS (`webapp/styles.css` ~254); the s40 attribution fix (`39918fe`) made it defunct.
  Remove the rule (rule removal, not file deletion) once confirmed no scenario still emits an
  unattributed lane header. (implementation-notes-s40-timeline-session-attribution)
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (won't-do — rule is load-bearing, premise wrong):** swept all 85 covered
  scenarios building each document + timeline view-model: 29 scenarios (s23, s29, s32, s34,
  s35, s37, s38, s41–s44, s50, s51, s54–s60, s62, s72–s75, s82–s85) each still emit exactly
  one unattributed agent-turn — the script-execution turns whose synthetic changeIds are
  per-replay `randomUUID()` (item 34). Removing the rule would re-show the "(unattrib" header
  in all 29. Re-check after item 34 lands.

title: `/api/document` runs its per-line progress walk twice per request
description:
32. `/api/document` runs its per-line progress walk twice per request** — once for the
  script-consent scan, once for the document build, both labeled "reusing cached"; the console
  reads as "loaded twice". Cosmetic. (handoff 0119, s40 notes)
  **Closed 2026-07-08:** the per-record walk now happens exactly once per request —
  `buildDocumentWithConsent`/`buildProjectDocument` no longer replay records
  (`src/viewer_api.ts`); the route's own `loadProjectRecords` call is the single walk.
  Contract tests rewritten in `tests/viewer-progress.test.ts`.

title: Filter command-message prompts from the timeline?
description:
33. Filter command-message prompts from the timeline?** — s39 renders 13 steps vs the
  sketch's 7 partly because `/ponytail`-style command prompts and their ack replies each get a
  numbered step (4 extra turns across 2 sessions). Filter them out, or keep as steps?
  (implementation-notes-turn-based-timeline-steps)
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (decided — keep):** command-message prompts and their ack replies stay
  as numbered steps, rendered dimmed via `checkMessageTextIsSystem`
  (`webapp/views/timeline.js:441`). Filtering them out would renumber steps and hide real
  turns. No code change.

title: Deterministic synthetic changeIds
description:
34. Deterministic synthetic changeIds** — the real fix for item 25's zero-chip turns:
  derive script-execution changeIds from target + run timestamp so the step timeline and
  file-history replays agree, instead of per-replay `randomUUID()`
  (`reconstruction_script_stage.ts:303`). Touches changeId-uniqueness assumptions; needs a
  user go-ahead. (implementation-notes-items13-19-21-25-close)
  **Closed 2026-07-08 (user-approved):** synthetic script-execution changeIds are now
  `scriptRun:<tool_use id | epoch-ms>:<target path>` via `computeScriptExecutionChangeId`
  (`src/reconstruction_script_execution.ts`; `ScriptRun` gained `toolUseId`), following the
  `originalFile:` prefix precedent. `resolveSyntheticChangeIdToSourceId` unwraps the new prefix
  via `resolveScriptRunChangeIdToSourceId`, so those steps also gain session attribution.
  `reconstruction_git_evidence.ts`'s randomUUID splice deliberately untouched (commit markers
  are the viewer's commit signal). 8 tests written (not run — user runs the suite); after the
  scenario sweep, re-check item 31's "(unattributed)" CSS rule.

title: Content-keyed memoization of `executeRunOnce`
description:
35. Content-keyed memoization of `executeRunOnce`** — if the branches-pass/steps-pass
  double reconstruction on real transcripts is still too costly after `f311059`'s
  lineage-window fix. Explicitly YAGNI until a new logs capture shows it matters.
  (implementation-notes-repeated-reconstruction-work)
  **Closed 2026-07-14 (YAGNI confirmed, no code written):** the trigger condition never fired —
  no capture shows `executeRunOnce` costing. Three findings, each independently sufficient:
  (a) the memo is *already* content-keyed on the run — `reconstruction_script_stage.ts` keys on
  `` `${run.timestamp.getTime()}|${run.code}` ``; only the outer cache scope
  (`getDerivedCaches(records, reader)`) is records-array identity, so the two passes miss each
  other's memo. Narrower than the item's title implies. (b) Item 68's read-only gate eats the
  work first: logs5 (2026-07-13, the only post-gate capture) shows **1810 read-only skips vs 114
  executions** — ~94% of runs never reach a sandbox. logs1–4 are all 2026-07-07, predating both

title: Add engine capabilities for handling customized paths for the following data sources
description:
46. Add engine capabilities for handling customized paths for the following data sources**: JSONL project path, File History Snapshot Path, git repo Path & git commit hash to use as the base commit, on-disk location of project where conversations took place.  when parsing JSONL files that have a CWD, the on-disk location path would override the extracted CWD.  File History Snapshot (FHS) path: when this argument is set, when a FHS path is detected in a JSONL file, the lookup process to get the correct FHS path would be: `<Custom_FHS_Path>/<JSONL_Session_UUID>/<FHS_hash@vN>`.
  **Closed 2026-07-09 (implemented; suite NOT run — user runs it):** new
  `src/reconstruction_overrides.ts` (process-wide override state on the exec-gate precedent,
  `{}` = today's exact behavior) + `src/reconstruction_base_commit.ts`. (1) FHS root chain:
  explicit override → `file-history/` sibling derived from the transcript's own on-disk
  location (`resolveFileHistoryRoot`, `reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts`) → `~/.claude`
  default; lookup stays `<root>/<sessionUuid>/<blob@vN>`; viewer serves/derives via
  `getEffectiveFileHistoryDir` and the header gains a prepopulated File-history field (an
  unedited field posts `""` so the server re-derives on folder switch). (2) per-project
  `reveng-paths.json` in the projects folder (project name → `{cwd, repo, baseCommit}`),
  read by the viewer per request (`applyProjectOverrides`, cache-stamped via
  `serializePathOverrides`) and by the CLI (`applyCliPathOverrides`; flags
  `--file-history-loc|--fhsLoc`, `--cwd`, `--repo`, `--base-commit` win per-field).
  (3) cwd/repo overrides join the git-evidence fallback chain (`findFallbackRepoDirs`) —
  DELIBERATE deviation from the parse-time-override wording (user-approved in-conversation):
  rewriting record.cwd breaks relpath math and lineage joins. (4) base commit = tier-1
  beacon: `seedBaseCommitBeacon` splices a `WriteEvent` of the committed bytes at the
  commit's timestamp (deterministic `gitBase:` changeIds; mid-session commits supersede
  earlier steps; user-specified semantics). 21 new tests across 5 files (written, not run);
  engine-efficiency follow-up is item 56. Plan: `plans/item46-custom-data-source-paths.md`.

title: Filter out read-only scripts in the script-execution phase
description:
68. Filter out read-only scripts in the script-execution phase** — the
  2026-07-11 profiling session found the dominant cold-load cost is sandbox
  execution of EVERY recorded script run (`discoverScriptCreatedPaths` executes
  all of them eagerly — 1000+ runs on the 33-session RevEng project, each
  seeding ~192 files into a temp dir), yet most recorded runs are read-only
  analysis scripts (ctx_execute grep/count/print) whose outcomes change no
  files. Add a static write-detection gate before `executeRunOnce`
  (reconstruction_script_stage.ts): skip the sandbox for a script whose code
  contains no write primitive (`open(..,"w"/"a")`, `shutil.*`, `os.rename`/
  `os.remove`, `pathlib .write_text/.write_bytes`, `writeFileSync`, shell
  redirects, `mkdir`, `mv`/`cp`/`rm`, ...). Validate the heuristic against the
  full scenario coverage harness (a false "read-only" verdict silently loses
  file evidence — the harness must stay green). Note the overlap with task
  #67's blocked prerequisite: the same classification ("does this run modify
  files") drives both; a static gate is its cheap approximation, an executed
  outcome (`execution.post` vs `pre`) its exact answer. Logged 2026-07-11
  during the JSONL-loading performance investigation (fixes 1-6: five corpus
  memos + sandbox memo capacity 256→4096 already landed that session).
  DONE 2026-07-11 — static gate `scriptCodeMayWriteFiles` (python-write-primitive
  tokens + stdlib-import allowlist + open-mode analysis) skips the pre-state build
  and sandbox in `executeRunOnce` and bails `runOutcomeForTarget` early; anything
  unparseable stays may-write (a false may-write only costs a sandbox run, never
  evidence; shell/JS scripts crash under python3 either way, so bare `>` shell
  tokens are deliberately omitted). Plan: plans/item68-readonly-script-gate.md.
  tsc clean; suite + scenario harness not run (user runs).

title: Indicate which scripts in Script Execution Consent view are read-only vs

description:
74. BUG: File Revision Panel's Diff View's "Columns" mode doesn't constrain its width to the window's width.   The '<div id="details-right">' element needs its width constrained to the right edge of the browser window and the content needs to be wrapped.
  **Closed 2026-07-13:** root cause was in the fork details-pane diff surface (`webapp/styles.css`
  `.diff-cols`), never converted when the sibling `diff-vs-base.ts` surface got the same fix in
  items 39/48. `.diff-cols` carried `min-width: max-content` (forcing the grid to its longest
  line) with `minmax(160px, 1fr)` text columns, and `.dc-body`/`.dc-hunk` used `white-space: pre`
  (no wrap) — so long diff lines overflowed `#details-right` and scrolled the pane. Fix (CSS-only):
  dropped `min-width: max-content`, switched text columns to `minmax(0, 1fr)`, and set the body +
  hunk cells to `white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere` — the exact item-39/48 pattern.
  Verified served live on 7343; visual/suite check is the user's standing pass. NOTE: the sibling
  Inline view on this same pane (`.diff` / `.diff-line`, also `min-width: max-content` + `pre`)
  shares the root cause and likely overflows too — left untouched as out of this task's scope.

title: "/dev/null" appearing as a file in the Files list
description:
76: "/dev/null" appearing as a file in the Files list.**
  **DONE 2026-07-13:** Root cause was `parseRedirect` in `src/reconstruction_extract.ts`: a
  command like `python build.py > /dev/null` (or `... 2>/dev/null`) was parsed as an overwrite
  of the file `/dev/null`, producing a real file event that surfaced in the Files list. Writing
  to `/dev/null` discards output and is never a file, so `parseRedirect` now returns `undefined`
  when the redirect target is the null device (new `NULL_DEVICE` guard, one check covering both
  `>` and `>>`). Not a sign of a bigger bug — the sibling idiom `> /dev/null 2>&1` already parsed
  to nothing. Added `test_parseRedirect_ignores_the_null_device` in tests/reconstruction_extract.test.ts.

title: Give the Files column a true File tree view, instead of the current full-path list view
description:
77: Give the Files column a true File tree view, instead of the current full-path list view.**
  The full paths are truncated anyway, so there's no real way to know what file is being loaded.
  Discovered in: http://127.0.0.1:7343/#/project/-Users-matkatmusicllc-Programming-jot-backup/timeline
  **DONE 2026-07-14:** The Files pane (`webapp/views/sidebar.ts`) is now a nested tree of native
  `<details open>` folders with **basename** leaves (full path moved to the `title` tooltip), instead
  of one flat `.file-item` per absolute path. The key finding: real targets are absolute and deep
  (`/private/var/folders/fy/…/T/run-scenario.9xxymp7j/alpha.py`), so a naive path-split tree would
  render ~8 single-child folders before the first file — worse than the flat list. `buildFileTree`
  therefore strips the directory prefix every target shares (`findCommonDirectoryPrefix`, compared
  **segment-wise**: `/foo/bar` and `/foo/barn` share only `/foo`, a character-wise prefix is a bug).
  Folders sort before files, each group alphabetical; every folder starts expanded (no toggle JS, no
  collapse state). Per the task's "Gotchas" line (a copy-paste artifact that belongs to 77, not 78)
  and the user's decisions: a **renamed** file shows once at its final path with a `← oldname` badge
  (the engine already keys a renamed file's history at its final path — `src/reconstruction_lineage.ts`
  — so `originalPath` comes from the first rename revision's `from`); a **deleted** file stays in the
  tree struck-through/dimmed (`isDeleted` = the **LAST** revision is a delete, so m4's
  write→delete→write recreate correctly reads as alive). **No engine/`src` change was needed** — the
  wire already carried every fact. `clearSidebarFileSelection` and its `timeline.ts` caller are
  untouched (leaves kept the `.file-item` class), and the call site changed by one argument.
  15 new tests in `tests/timeline-viewmodels.test.ts` (98 pass / 0 fail in that file); both typechecks
  and `build:webapp` clean. Also removed dead `.tree-file` CSS (referenced by no TS; preserved in
  `webapp/archive/styles-pre-item66.css`). Plan: `plans/item77-files-tree-view.md`; notes:
  `plans/implementation-notes-item77-files-tree-view.md`. User runs the full suite + visual pass.
  Possible follow-ups (deliberately skipped, see notes): a header row naming the stripped common
  root; migrating `project.ts`'s single-level `groupTargetsByDirectory` pane to the same builder.

title: make `builtDocumentCache` disk-backed so respawns skip reconstruction and finish faster during development.  Discovered in: http://127.0.0.1:7343/#/project/-Users-matkatmusicllc-Programming-jot-backup/timeline
description:
79:  make `builtDocumentCache` disk-backed so respawns skip reconstruction and finish faster during development.  Discovered in: http://127.0.0.1:7343/#/project/-Users-matkatmusicllc-Programming-jot-backup/timeline
  **DONE 2026-07-13:** new `src/reconstruction_document_cache.ts` persists each `BuiltReconstruction`
  to `.cache/built-documents/<sha256(cacheKey)>.json`, opt-in like item 11's sandbox memo (only
  `viewer_server.ts` configures it; CLI/tests stay memory-only). `buildReconstructionWithConsent`
  reads disk on an in-memory miss (hydrate → repopulate memory → return) and writes disk after a
  fresh build. `--resetDocumentCache` flag added. **Two deviations from the handoff, both leaner +
  more robust (user-approved):** (1) serialize/hydrate is ONE type-driven tag replacer/reviver — the
  replacer reaches past `toJSON` via the holder (`this[key]`) to `instanceof`-tag Path/Uuid/Date, so
  3 branches cover the whole tree and it survives any document shape change — NOT ~13 hand-written
  per-type hydrators. The handoff's "a generic replacer can't work" was true only of a value-only
  replacer; the holder trick refutes it (proven empirically). (2) eviction is by on-disk mtime
  (`DOCUMENT_CACHE_CAPACITY = 4`), not an in-memory LRU the filesystem already records. Audit
  confirmed every persisted field bottoms out in Path/Uuid/Date + JSON primitives (no Maps/Sets/
  cycles). Round-trip correctness test in `tests/reconstruction_document_cache.test.ts` asserts a
  hydrated build drives `resolveFilesAtStep` byte-identically to a fresh build. Both typechecks
  clean; suite left for the user. Plan: `plans/item79-disk-backed-document-cache.md`.
  **Measured 2026-07-13 (user asked to measure first):** on the large RevEng project (30,201
  records, 87.2 MB document), a cold respawn — cold in-memory caches, WARM disk sandbox memo
  (item 11) — spends parse 391 ms + reconstruction **468,094 ms (~7.8 min)**. Emphatically NOT
  YAGNI: a disk-backed document cache turns that into a sub-second disk read + JSON.parse.
  **Decision: build FULL-FIDELITY** (persist `document` + `stepFileHistories` with a
  FileHistory/FileRevision hydration layer, so every route — incl. range-patch/step-files —
  skips the rebuild on respawn). STILL TO DO — not yet implemented.
  **Design note for next session:** a plain JSON.parse of the persisted value is NOT enough —
  server code calls Path domain methods on the built values (e.g. `findFileHistory` calls
  `entry.target.equals()` on `document.filesTouched`), so both `document` (its embedded
  `filesTouched`/`rewoundFilesTouched`/`steps` FileHistory + Path/Date fields) AND
  `stepFileHistories` need structure-aware hydration back into `Path`/`Date`/`Uuid` domain
  objects (`src/structures/domain.ts`). `FileRevision` (`src/reconstruction_engine.ts:48`) and
  `FileHistory` (`:58`) field shapes still need a full audit before writing the hydrator.
  Suggested shape: new `src/reconstruction_document_cache.ts` (opt-in like item 11's
  `configureSandboxMemoPersistence`; only `viewer_server.ts` enables it, CLI/tests stay
  memory-only), one file per cacheKey under `.cache/built-documents/` (gitignored), LRU-capped,
  with a schema-version tag so a shape change invalidates old files. Key already safe across
  restarts (transcript mtime+size stamp + allowScripts + target + `serializePathOverrides()`).
  Round-trip hydration test (build a small scenario → serialize → hydrate → assert range-patch/
  step-files output identical to a fresh build) is the required correctness gate.

title: console should word-wrap lines that are longer than the console's width in the browser window
description:
80: console should word-wrap lines that are longer than the console's width in the browser window.
  **DONE 2026-07-13:** root cause was xterm `cols` drifting out of sync with the console's
  real width — xterm autowraps at `cols`, but `fitProgressColumns` only re-fit on
  `window.resize` + console-expand, so a width change with no resize event (dragging the
  sidebar↔rightcol splitter `#split-lr`, or a zero-width initial fit leaving xterm at its
  default 80 cols) left `cols` wider than the visible console and long lines overflowed
  (clipped by `overflow: hidden`), looking un-wrapped. Fix: a `ResizeObserver` on
  `#progress-console` re-fits `cols` on every box change (`webapp/app.ts`,

  { overflow: hidden }` clipped it below the fold, so scrollToBottom couldn't help. Fix: resize

title: progress indicator overhaul
description:
82: progress indicator overhaul — done (plan `plans/item82-loading-progress-overhaul.md`,
  notes `plans/implementation-notes-item82-loading-progress-overhaul.md`). A real capture of
  `/api/document?progress=1` for `-Users-matkatmusicllc-Programming-jot-backup` (mockup:
  `mockups/loading-progress.html`) proved the "frozen 5s+" is NOT the build stages — it's the
  **67.1 MB document**: 20,418 per-record parse lines flood in ~2.6s, then the console freezes on
  "reusing cached document artifact" for ~4s warm / 33s cold while the server `JSON.stringify`s
  67 MB and the browser `JSON.parse`s it — both outside any progress line. Fix, reusing the
  existing NDJSON stream / `showLoadingProgress` (no new transport): (a) server brackets the two
  silent blocking steps with honest lines `serializing document` + `sending document (N MB)`
  (`viewer_server.ts`, `viewer_api.ts`); (b) the cache-hit per-record replay is throttled from one
  line/record to ≤50 counted, still token-bearing lines (`computeRecordProgressStride` in
  `viewer_api.ts`); (c) the client indicator is now always-visible with a ticking elapsed clock, a
  phase-N-of-6 header + bar (`classifyLoadPhase`), a determinate stage bar when counted and an
  animated shimmer when not, and a `parsing document — N MB` label + paint-yield before the
  terminal `JSON.parse` (`webapp/app.ts`, `webapp/styles.css`). The 67 MB payload itself and the
  cold per-record parse flood are deliberately left as separate follow-ups. Client behaviour is the
  user's standing visual-verify (console/overlay convention); pure helpers covered by
  `tests/loading-progress.test.ts`.

title: unify the bottom pane for ALL file-related content
description:
84: unify the bottom pane for ALL file-related content** — **IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-14**
  (staged, uncommitted; notes: `plans/implementation-notes-item84-unify-bottom-pane.md`, plan:
  `plans/item84-unify-bottom-pane.md`). Every chip-row button is now a deep-link into
  `renderDetailsFileMode`, which gained a `focus?: RevisionFocus` param ({changeId, mode}) plus a
  `RevisionViewMode` enum (diff/content/record): chip name → content, `+/-` → diff, `{ }` → the
  causing record (rev cards stay standing for free — `openInspectorPane` never touches
  `#details-left`), `⤷` untouched. Rev cards gained a 6th `{ }` action and a `☐`/`☑` range toggle;
  a contiguous run renders the step-range diff moved out of `showFilePreview`. NET DELETION:
  `showFilePreview`, `showRevisionDiff`, `toggleDrawerButton`, `fetchStepFiles` + 3 imports retired
  (commented, not deleted). 11 new tests in `tests/details-revision-view.test.ts`; typecheck +
  `build:webapp` clean. 3 factual errors in this item's own pre-implementation text were corrected
  first (⤷ resolves the chip's OWN changeId; `showRevisionDiffInDetails` SURVIVES — it has a live
  caller in `appendFileList`; `{ }`'s meaning is unchanged but its rendering is not). Dropped:
  click-again-to-close, and chip-click-while-steps-are-picked. Client behavior is the user's
  standing visual-verify. Original description follows:
  The bottom pane must display
  file-related content in exactly ONE gui, whether you got there from the Files treeview or from a
  timeline node's file chip. There is one view — the Revision View — and every route into it is the
  same three choices: **which file, which revision selection (one card, or a contiguous run of
  cards), which right-column mode**. Nothing else renders file content anywhere.
  **The rule:** every timeline chip-row button is a deep-link into the Revision View. Chip button X
  ≡ `click treeview entry → click that revision's card → click the card's X`. The left column always
  shows the `.rev-card` list with the chip's revision selected; only the right column differs.
  **Today it's two renderers.** The treeview click runs `renderDetailsFileMode`
  (`webapp/views/details.ts:372`) and rewrites BOTH columns — rev cards in `#details-left`, the
  selected revision's diff in `#details-right`. The chip click runs a separate renderer,
  `showFilePreview` (`webapp/views/timeline.ts:1526`), which touches only `#details-right-body` and
  leaves `#details-left` showing the previously-selected row's file list — stale and unrelated to
  the clicked chip. This is not "build a lookalike": it is deleting the second renderer and calling
  the first. Each chip carries its own `changeId` (one chip per change, not per file), and
  `findRevisionForChangeId` already resolves `changeId` → revision index, so the revision to select
  is never ambiguous.
  - **Chip click** → `treeview entry → revision card → Show content`. Keeps the chip's meaning
    (file content at that revision), now in the real Revision View. Deletes `showFilePreview`.
  - **`+/-`** → `treeview entry → revision card`, nothing further: clicking a card IS how you view
    that revision's diff today, so the card's default right-column render already IS `+/-`'s
    meaning. Deletes `showRevisionDiff` (`timeline.ts:1595`), which
    also retires its near-duplicate twin `showRevisionDiffInDetails` (`details.ts:301`) — same
    `/api/diff?mode=revisions` call, same `splitDiffBlocks`, same fallback, two hand-rolled lookups,
    two fetch caches.
  - **`{ }`** → `treeview entry → revision card → the card's { }`. Keeps its MEANING (the file's own
    causing JSONL record — still the only route to a file-modifying event's JSON, not a duplicate of
    anything) but NOT its rendering: the record paints into the revision details pane with the rev
    cards still shown. It must not take the pane over or navigate away, which is what today's
    `openTranscriptInspectorSynced(causingLocation)` (`timeline.ts:1649`) does. Synthetic-changeId
    chips keep the existing `openTurnInspector` fallback (`timeline.ts:1646`).
  - **Rev cards gain a `{ }` button** as a 6th action, after `Jump to timeline step`
    (`buildRevisionCards`, `details.ts:72`; cards built at `details.ts:430-457`). This is the button
    the chip's `{ }` now delegates to — so it is load-bearing for the rule above, not a nicety.
    Without it the Revision View has no JSON route at all.
  - **`⤷`** (Jump to File History Snapshot) → UNTOUCHED, user-decided. Its value is its *presence*:
    `computeSnapshotJumpRoute` returns `undefined` → no button, so absence signals "no File History
    Snapshot for this revision". It navigates to the File History route — a separate surface, not
    bottom-pane content. (CORRECTION to this item's earlier text: it resolves
    `findRevisionForChangeId(files, change.changeId, undefined)` — the chip's OWN changeId, the same
    revision `+/-` resolves. It does NOT vary the revision.)
  - Gotcha: `openInspectorPane` (`inspector.ts:353`) force-hides the diff-mode toggle and pins the
    label to "JSON"; a naive swap inherits that wrong chrome.
  - **Step-range diff → contiguous multi-card selection.** `showFilePreview`'s per-file range diff
    (when steps are picked, `timeline.ts:1532-1544`) does NOT get dropped — it moves into the
    Revision View as a 4th right-column mode, hung on a multi-card selection: rev cards gain toggle
    buttons, and selecting a **contiguous** run of cards renders that range's diff. Non-contiguous
    selections are rejected. This is why the rule's middle term is a revision *selection*, not a
    single revision — single card and contiguous run are the same mechanism at N=1 and N>1.
    (NOT BUILT: chip click while a step range is picked seeding that run — never requested; see the
    implementation notes.)

description: The FIRST commit of a session ("baseline") shows "No files changed" + no contrib rows: its file chips live on the trailing reply bubble that sorts AFTER the commit row (snapshot attribution), so the walk-back finds nothing. Later commits work. Acceptable, or should `deriveCommitChangedFiles` also absorb the files bubble immediately after the commit? (item 66)
closureNote: Closed per user decision (fix it): deriveCommitChangedFiles now also walks FORWARD to the next commit, absorbing chips whose change instant is at-or-before the commit (the trailing reply bubble that sorts after the commit row), and skips gitBase baseline chips in both directions; findContributingNodeIndexes mirrors the same walk so the highlight agrees.

title: Rev-card op badges: single letters (A/M) vs the mockup's word badges
description: Rev-card op badges render single letters (A/M) rather than the mockup's word badges (write/edit/user-edit) — eyeball and decide which reads better. (item 66) Location: `webapp/views/timeline.ts:1183–1217` (`op-badge` span) + a styles.css width tweak. Confirm with the user before styling choices.

The single letters live only on the timeline file chips (computeOpLetter, timeline.ts) — deliberate compact design, kept per user decision. title: s39 emits NO commit node: compound `git add … && git commit` extracts only the add op
description: PROBLEM: the s39 transcript runs `git add … && git commit` as one compound Bash command, but git-op extraction only recognizes the `add` op from compound commands, so the reconstructed timeline emits NO commit node for s39 — the commit is invisible in the viewer even though it happened. This is pre-existing engine behavior, not an item-66 port regression. NEEDED: either extend git-op extraction to recognize each op in `&&`-chained compound commands (so the commit gets its own node), or explicitly decide and document that compound-command commits are out of scope. (item 66)
closureNote: Closed per user decision (extend extraction). PREMISE CORRECTION: s39's transcript records NO `git commit` at all — a block-compound.sh capture hook forced separate commands and only `git init` + `git add orders.py tests/` exist in its JSONLs, so no s39 commit node was ever recoverable; the compound-command gap was real but lives in s6-git-mv (`git add … && git commit -m "$(cat …)"`). FIX: splitCompoundCommandSegments in src/reconstruction_git_evidence.ts — both findGitOperations and findGitCommitEvents now parse each `&&` segment (per-segment kind/detail/command; commit segments read the compound's single tool_result for resultHash; -C dir read from the commit's own segment). s6's kind sequence gains its compound commit: [init, add, commit, add, commit, other]. 3 new tests across tests/git-operations.test.ts and tests/reconstruction_git_evidence.test.ts.

title: Files tree, multi-root projects: collapse single-child chains below the root?
description: PROBLEM: in multi-root projects (sessions ran under different `cwd`s), the files-tree root is the shallow shared prefix (e.g. `/Users/matkatmusicllc`), so real single-child directory chains survive below it (`Programming` → `jot-backup` → `src`). Each intermediate level holds exactly one child, so navigating the tree costs one click per level that carries no information. This is honest divergence, not a reconstruction bug. NEEDED: decide whether to collapse single-child chains *below* the root into one combined node (e.g. `Programming/jot-backup/src`). Note: root-level chain-collapsing was previously declined, so this needs explicit sign-off that below-root collapsing is wanted. (item 77)
closureNote: User signed off on below-root collapsing (root-level stays declined). Implemented collapseSingleChildFolderChains post-pass in buildFileTree (webapp/views/timeline.ts): each folder holding exactly one folder child merges into a combined a/b/c node, stopping at branching folders and file children. 3 new tests in tests/timeline-viewmodels.test.ts; 755 tests green.

title: Rename badge shows only the old basename — ambiguous for same-basename renames
description:
PROBLEM: the rename badge shows only `← <old basename>`, with the full old path relegated to the tooltip. When two files in different directories were renamed from the same basename, their badges are visually identical — the user cannot tell the renames apart without hovering each one. NEEDED: disambiguate inline, e.g. show the shortest distinguishing suffix of the old path (only when two badges would otherwise collide, or always), or decide the tooltip is sufficient and close. (item 77)
 DECISION: disamiguate inline.
closureNote: Rename badges now disambiguate inline: applyRenameBadgeLabels grows colliding old-basename badges to the shortest distinguishing suffix (sidebar + details pane, pane-local on copies). Suite green. Work staged, not yet committed (add the commit hash when committing).

title: Split oversized files: webapp/views/timeline.ts, webapp/views/details.ts, tests/timeline-viewmodels.test.ts
description: `tests/timeline-viewmodels.test.ts` (2017 lines), `webapp/views/timeline.ts` (2071 lines), and `webapp/views/details.ts` (623 lines) all trip the project's 250-line file-size hook, which also flags pre-existing deep nesting. None of it originates from items 77/84, and splitting is a large refactor outside those tasks — but the ledger keeps growing, so it deserves its own item. (items 77 + 84) ALSO: src/reconstruction_git_evidence.ts is 568 lines vs the 250-line hook cap (plus one deep-nesting site around `placementAfter`) — pre-existing before task 89's compound-extraction change, flagged by the jot post-edit hook on every edit.
closureNote: Closed by the codebase-wide oversize split (user-expanded scope): audited all 153 tracked TS files via the jot hook's own filesize_check.py, then split every file over the 250-line cap — the four named files (timeline.ts 2266->220+14 modules, timeline-viewmodels.test.ts 2364->17 topic files, details.ts 685->4 modules, reconstruction_git_evidence.ts 558->3 modules) plus 26 more src/webapp/tests files (~35 new modules total, incl. app.ts 1219->10 modules). Pure moves, no re-export shims, callers import canonical homes directly. typecheck + build:webapp green; test suite deliberately left for the user to run. Deep-nesting hook flags recorded in plans/implementation-notes-task-92.md as follow-up input. Staged, not committed.

title: renderFileHistoryView is a near-duplicate of the Revision View — consolidate?
description:
PROBLEM: two views implement the same per-revision UI independently. `renderFileHistoryView` (`webapp/views/file-history.ts:161`, route `#/project/

/file/`) renders per-revision rows with the *same five actions* as the Revision View's rev cards (Show content / Export this version / Copy patch / Export .patch / Jump to timeline step). Since item 84's bug-1 fix removed its `⤷` chip-row entry point, it is reachable only from the inspector's revision links and the snapshot pane's "View in File History" button — yet every future change to the five actions must be made in both places. NEEDED: consolidate — either retire `renderFileHistoryView` and repoint its two remaining entry points at the Revision View, or extract the shared revision-row rendering into one helper both views call. (item 84)
closureNote:
Option 1 implemented (user decision): renderFileHistoryView archived to webapp/archive/file-history-pre-task93.ts; the #/project/

/file/[/rev/] route now renders THE Revision View (renderDetailsFileMode) via the timeline's exported activeDetailsContext, with computeFileRouteFocus mapping the /rev/ anchor to a content-mode RevisionFocus (4 new tests); the Diff-vs-Base entry button moved into the Revision View. Staged, not committed.

title: `⤷` snapshot-jump button renders for any matched changeId, not only snapshot-backed revisions
description:
PROBLEM: the `⤷` snapshot-jump button is supposed to signal "this revision HAS a File History Snapshot", but its render condition doesn't check that. It renders whenever `computeSnapshotJumpRoute` returns a route, and that returns `undefined` only when the changeId is absent, resolves to no history, or resolves to a blob name with no anchored revision — i.e. the button appears for essentially any changeId that matches a revision, snapshot-backed or not. The indicator over-fires and misleads. NEEDED: tighten the render condition so `⤷` appears only for revisions actually backed by a snapshot, or redefine/document the button's meaning as "jumpable" rather than "snapshot-backed". (item 84)
DECISION: Tighten the render condition so `⤷` appears only for revisions actually backed by a snapshot, replace snapshot-button graphic with the camera emoji icon, add a tool tip that reads "Show this specific File History Snapshot in File Revisions view".
closureNote: Snapshot-jump button now renders only for snapshot-backed revisions (backup-blob @vN changeIds, gated in computeSnapshotJumpRoute), with camera emoji and tooltip 'Show this specific File History Snapshot in File Revisions view'. Suite green. Work staged, not yet committed (add the commit hash when committing).

title: Doubled rtk-rewrite tool-call rows (s39): signal, or collapse into the original row?
description:
PROBLEM: when the rtk-rewrite hook rewrites a tool call, the timeline renders two rows for one logical action — the original and the rewrite. In s39 the hook rewrote both `ls` and `git add`, so the timeline shows `* git add … *` AND `* rtk git add … *`. This follows the locked "all tool calls, including hook rewrites" rule, but the doubled rows may read as noise rather than signal. NEEDED: decide whether doubled hook-rewrite rows stay as-is (two rows = signal) or a rewrite collapses into its original row (one row, two line labels); if collapsing, implement it in the timeline tool-call row rendering. (timeline tool-call rows)
 DECISION: keep the doubled rows.
closureNote: Resolved by decision, no code change: the doubled rows (original + rtk-rewrite tool call) are the intended signal per the locked "all tool calls, including hook rewrites" rule; the user decided to keep them as-is.

title: Failed git commands still emit timeline rows and CommitMarkers — suppress or badge?
description:
PROBLEM: git-op extraction never checks `is_error`, so a FAILED git command still contributes timeline rows. s6's compound `git add … && git commit` failed at runtime yet now contributes add+commit rows (its commit row has `resultHash: undefined` — error output carries no `[branch hash]` line); this mirrors how a failed plain `git commit` already gets a row today. Relatedly, `findGitCommitEvents` for s6 returns 2 commit events (failed compound + retry) where the repo has only 1 real commit — `resolveCommitByTimestamp` resolves both to the same commit (harmless for the evidence channel), but CommitMarkers (timeline pick hard-stops) now include the failed compound's instant; flag if a duplicate marker ever shows up as a visible artifact in the viewer. NEEDED: decide whether failed git commands should be suppressed or badged — a decision spanning ALL git ops, not just compound ones. 
DECISION: Badge failed git commands as 'FAILED' (red) in the timeline.
closureNote: Failed git commands (tool_result is_error) now stamp GitOperation.isError through the wire onto commit nodes and their Bash tool-call rows, rendered as a red FAILED badge; rows are badged, never suppressed. Suite green. Work staged, not yet committed (add the commit hash when committing).

title: Script-run details: script + before/after diff panels

NEEDED: for script runs that modify files, the Details pane shows two panels — left: the script itself; right: a side-by-side diff of each affected file before vs. after the run. BLOCKED on a prerequisite that doesn't exist yet: the engine has script-run rows but no "this run changed files X, Y" linkage to drive the diff panel. title: Partial reconstruction: surface recoverable file states even when full reconstruction fails
description:
Add "reconstruct up to..." functionality even if the full reconstruction fails. The reconstruction engine should be able to provide at least SOME reconstructed file states from the JSONL files it finds, even if the entire session cannot be reconstructed. The engine and webapp need a way to reflect this reconstruction state so the user knows what file states were recoverable and what were not.

Scope (refined with user):
- Failure modes to survive (all three): (1) parser-level crashes — unknown record types/keys in newer-CC JSONLs must not abort the load; skip the bad record, keep parsing, reconstruct from what loaded (today an unknown record type crashes the viewer before the consent dialog); (2) engine-stage failures — a reconstruction stage throwing mid-session keeps all file states computed up to that point; (3) missing-evidence gaps — sidecar backups / git repo / recorded tmpdir gone: reconstruct the revisions that don't need the missing evidence, mark the rest unrecoverable.
- Granularity: per-revision. Each revision of each file is marked recovered or unrecoverable, with a reason (matches the per-step coverage-ledger mindset).
- Webapp UI (chosen A+C from mockups in plans/partial-reconstruction-ui-mockups.html): session-level partial-reconstruction banner with counts; inline dashed gap rows in the timeline; dashed/grayed missing rev-cards in the revision stepper; plus a per-file coverage strip in the file list (one segment per revision, red = unrecoverable, click a red segment for a reason popover). Same engine output feeds both treatments.
closureNote: Implemented 2026-07-19 across engine + webapp: tolerant parsing captures SkippedLines, a reconstruction_health failure sink survives per-stage/per-event/per-file/per-phase throws (unrecoverable placeholder revisions carry prior content forward), and the webapp renders the A+C treatments (banner, dashed gap rows, missing rev-cards, coverage strips with reason popovers). Both tsconfigs typecheck clean; committed by the user as jfred 3b01c62, superproject fa4ef2f. No failure-path fixture exists yet (task 83 not started), but the user verified s87 loads intact through the new tolerant/tolerance code paths and closed the task on that basis. Two open questions live in the implementation notes: a possible CLI --tolerant flag, and whether clicking a missing rev-card should show the reason instead of the carried-forward diff.

title: Timeline: toggle to show every JSONL line as a row (restore the pre-filter-chips view)
description: Add a way to toggle visibility of every JSONL line in the timeline — the original jfred view that showed each transcript line as a row disappeared when filter chips/filtering were added. The current filter (jfred/webapp/views/timeline-filter-model.ts, checkNodeMatchesFilterMode; DOM in timeline-render-filterbar.ts) is a display filter over already-built nodes, and 'All' already shows every NODE — but nodes are derived from structured wire collections (buildTurnTimelineViewModel in timeline-nodes.ts, deriveCommitNodes/deriveToolCallNodes in timeline-node-derive.ts), so non-turn/non-tool/non-git JSONL lines are never nodes at all; a new filter mode alone does nothing. (1) Row-level button: appendJsonRecordButton (jfred/webapp/views/timeline-render-row-cells.ts:119, called from timeline-render-rows.ts:113); the only exclusion today is COMMIT_NODE_KIND at the call site, and the baseline node is AGENT_TURN_NODE_KIND with isGitBaseline: true and no uuid (built by recordGitBaselineSnapshot, timeline-nodes.ts:69). (2) Per-file chip button (s85, expanding the baseline row's file-touched rows): renderFileButtonRow (jfred/webapp/views/timeline-render-chips.ts:181) renders [{ }] whenever change.changeId is defined — baseline files carry a SYNTHETIC gitbase: changeId, causingLocation resolves undefined, and the click falls back to openTurnInspector showing 'no transcript line for this step (synthetic change id)' (showCausingRecordForChip, timeline-render-chips.ts:129). NOTE task-121 (decided) merges the baseline turn into its base-commit row where one exists — the commit row already suppresses the row-level button, but the per-file chips ride along, so site (2) matters in both shapes.

title: Paths... popover: add git repo picker + visual commit picker (engine inputs unreachable from the webapp)
description:
There is no way to specify the git repo and base commit hash engine inputs from the webapp — today they only come from <projectsDir>/reveng-paths.json (PROJECT_PATHS_CONFIG_NAME, jfred/src/reconstruction_overrides.ts:50; wire shape WireProjectPaths { cwd?, repo?, baseCommit? } at :53), applied per-request in viewer_api_projects.ts:86 and consumed by seedBaseCommitBeacon (reconstruction_base_commit.ts). Add to the Paths... picker (#paths-popover in jfred/webapp/index.html, wiring in app-header.ts initializeHeader):
(1) Repo path input — reuse the existing /api/pick-folder native-picker pattern (pickFolderInto, app-header.ts:106).
(2) COMMIT PICKER (decided 2026-07-20): once the repo path is chosen, show the repo's commit list visually and let the user pick the base commit from it — a new server route (e.g. /api/repo-commits?repo=…) runs `git log --format=<hash|date|subject>` and the popover renders a scrollable pick list; the picked hash fills baseCommit. No free-text-only hash entry.
MATCHING CAVEAT (decided 2026-07-20): the repo need NOT be the project's own folder — e.g. the ~/Programming/jot project will use the ~/Programming/jot-recovery/ repo. File paths RELATIVE to each root are what 'match': JSONL-recorded absolute paths under the project root must map to the same relative paths under the chosen repo root, even though the roots differ. The engine already remaps cwd (WireProjectPaths.cwd / s87 cwd-remap mechanism) — the commit-content lookup (readCommitFileContent, reconstruction_base_commit.ts:66, keyed by relativePath) relies on that relative-path agreement; surface a soft warning in the picker when few JSONL file paths resolve inside the picked commit's tree.
PERSISTENCE PROMPT (added 2026-07-20): when the user picks a CUSTOM repo path or file-history-snapshot path, ask whether to store the custom path(s) — on yes, write them into the project's reveng-paths.json entry (repo/baseCommit; decide whether an explicit file-history override belongs there too or stays server-session-only). No silent writes: picking a path applies it to the session either way, storing is the opt-in step. Same prompt applies to the file-history field in task 136's show/hide flow.
Design decision still open: projectsDir/fileHistoryDir are GLOBAL config (POST /api/config) but repo/baseCommit are PER-PROJECT overrides in reveng-paths.json — the UI likely needs to write the current project's entry in that file (new server route) rather than extend /api/config; the persistence prompt above is the natural trigger for that route. TRAP (task 56): the repo path in reveng-paths.json is jfred-root-relative, not absolute — decide which form the input accepts and normalize server-side.
closureNote: Implemented in jfred@017da9c: per-project repo input + visual commit pick list (/api/repo-commits), soft path-match warning (/api/repo-commit-match), and apply-to-session vs opt-in store (/api/project-paths) writing repo/baseCommit/fileHistory into reveng-paths.json.

title: Bug: projects listed twice on the #/ landing page (overlapping renderRoute race)
description: Visiting http://127.0.0.1:7343/#/ shows every project row twice — INTERMITTENT: with a small/fast projects folder (jfred/scenarios/executed) the list appears once; duplication shows with slower folders. That timing dependence fits the race: if the second renderRoute starts after the first finished, its replaceChildren wipes the first's rows (no dupes); only when the /api/projects fetch is slow enough for the two runs to overlap do both appends land. The server scan is dupe-free (scanProjects, jfred/src/viewer_api_projects.ts:118 — one listing per readdir directory entry), so the duplication is client-side: renderRoute (jfred/webapp/app-router.ts:47) clears the view synchronously (view.replaceChildren() at :50) then AWAITS renderProjectsView (jfred/webapp/views/projects.ts), which appends — two overlapping renderRoute calls each clear-then-append, and both appends land. Known double-trigger: the folder-change handler in app-header.ts:101-102 sets location.hash = '#/' (fires hashchange → renderRoute via app.ts:66) AND calls renderRoute() explicitly; boot also has initializeHeader().then(renderRoute) at app.ts:81. Fix at the shared spot, not per trigger: make renderRoute latest-wins (generation counter checked after each await; stale runs bail before touching the DOM) — that also covers slow /api/projects responses racing a fast navigation.
closureNote: Fixed: renderRoute is latest-wins — each run renders into a fresh pane swapped atomically into #view (stale runs append into a detached pane) plus a generation counter guarding shared chrome; covered by tests/app-router.test.ts. Staged in jfred, awaiting commit.

title: Bug: shell `mv` script run classified read-only (item-68 gate is Python-only)
description: In s2-move-file, the JSONL line-74 run `mv <tmp>/s2_original.py <tmp>/s2_moved.py` is shown as read-only, but it modifies files. Cause: the item-68 static gate scriptCodeMayWriteFiles (jfred/src/reconstruction_script_prestate.ts:94) only detects PYTHON write constructs — pythonWritePrimitive (jfred/src/regex_script_detection.ts) matches `.rename(`/`.write_text(`/etc., and a bare shell command has no matching token, safe imports, no open() calls → classified read-only. The wire flag comes from viewer_api.ts:92 (ConsentScript.readOnly, item 69); the engine side also skips the sandbox for such runs (reconstruction_script_runs.ts:88, PROGRESS_LABEL_READ_ONLY_SKIP_PREFIX). Correctness of reconstruction is unaffected (plain mv renames come from the dedicated rename extraction, and a shell script would crash the python3 sandbox anyway — see the prestate.ts:89 comment), but the read-only LABEL is wrong and misleading in the UI. Fix per the item-68 rule (narrow read-only, never widen): add a shell write-verb check (\b(?:mv|cp|rm|mkdir|touch|tee|ln|sed -i)\b, plus > / >> redirects) so shell mutation commands classify may-write; cost is only a wasted sandbox attempt on those runs.
closureNote: Fixed: new shellWritePrimitive regex (mv/cp/rm/mkdir/touch/tee/ln, sed -i, file-path redirects; 2>&1 and /dev/null stay read-only) wired as the first check in scriptCodeMayWriteFiles; covered by regex_script_detection + prestate tests. Staged in jfred, awaiting commit.

title: JSON details view: 'line 0/98' counter is ambiguous (0-based index over max-index)

title: Script-run row: 'modified 6 files' pill counts paths, not files (rename pairs double-counted)

Prefer collapsing — 'modified 3 files' matches what the user sees in the diff pane.

title: Investigate: s85 script renames missing from the Files nav ('core_one.py <- one.py (renamed)' badge absent)
description: In s85-git-commit-csv-and-move-scripts, files renamed by the script (one.py -> core_one.py etc. via shutil.move) do not show the rename representation in the Files nav column that other projects get (rename badge: renameBadgeLabel stamped by applyRenameBadgeLabels, jfred/webapp/views/timeline-file-tree.ts:45, fed by each history revision's rename?.from — see also renamedFrom in details.ts:56). Likely engine-side: the file tree only shows a badge when the file's history contains a rename REVISION; s85's evidence flows through beaconlessScriptExecutions + the git-commit BLOB channel (reconstruction_git_evidence.ts, placeGitCommitEvidence — see s85 ground truth), which may seed the renamed file's history at its final path with no rename revision. CHECK FIRST (known s85 HAZARD): the s85 repo is resolved via the recorded TEMP cwd (/var/folders/.../run-scenario.*) — if that tmpdir was cleaned, s85 reconstruction regresses wholesale and this symptom (plus task 146) may just be that regression, not a new gap. Run the CLI sweep on s85 before touching the webapp.
closureNote: Investigated and fixed: not the tmpdir hazard (checker 10/10 without it) — the surviving-trunk walk dropped parallel-tool-call sibling records (shared message.id), starving script discovery so core_*.py had no histories; absorbParallelToolCallSiblings restores them (plumbing-only subtree gate keeps real rewinds dimmed) and the Files sidebar badges script moves from renamedPaths. Rename REVISIONS for moved-away sources filed as follow-up in the implementation notes. Staged in jfred, awaiting commit.

title: Investigate: two.py absent from the Files nav in s85 (write at L48 confirmed in transcript)

title: Filter/find by conversation name in multi-JSONL projects (session custom titles)
description: Add a way to filter or find conversations by their user-given name in multi-JSONL projects. Motivating use case: locate the 'tackle 121' conversation in the RevEng projects dir to inspect the tool-result JSON from the agent's close-tasks 121 invocation. The data plumbing ALREADY exists end-to-end: custom-title records ({type:'custom-title', customTitle, sessionId}) are parsed into document.sessionTitles (findSessionTitles, jfred/src/reconstruction_json.ts:131/:241; wire field :149) and the webapp reads them (timeline-types.ts:92; session-header rows + timeline-labels.ts / timeline-render-row-cells.ts consumers). Behavior is UNDECIDED — candidate shapes, cheapest first: (1) include session titles in the existing task-127 timeline search index so typing 'tackle 121' jumps to that session's header row (zero new UI); (2) a session dropdown in the timeline header listing sessionTitles, jump-to-session-header on pick; (3) a filter chip that hides rows whose node.sessionId belongs to non-matching sessions (nodes already carry sessionId). Note the original 'chip for JSONL lines that have customTitle' framing would only match the title records themselves — the useful unit is the SESSION the title names, so filter/jump by sessionId. Decide the shape when picking this up; (1) likely satisfies the motivating search on its own.
closureNote: Implemented shape (1): session custom titles joined the task-127 timeline search. computeSessionTitleByNodeIndex maps each titled session to its FIRST node via findSessionStartIndexes; the search predicates take an optional sessionTitle so typing a title jumps to (and keeps visible) the row directly under that session-start marker. Five red-first tests in tests/timeline-filter-model-session-titles.test.ts (new file — the old test file sits at the 250-line cap). Staged in jfred, awaiting commit.

title: Progress UI goes silent for minutes inside 'Phase 4 of 6' on large real sessions
description: Loading the real RevEng project (#/project/-Users-matkatmusicllc-Desktop-claude-code-src-RevEng/timeline) sat in 'Phase 4 of 6' for 500+ seconds with the progress line frozen at '451/451 reconstructing <target>' — the counter reaches N/N and then nothing updates while the long tail runs. Emitter: reportReconstructionProgress fires once per target BEFORE its reconstructFileOver call (jfred/src/reconstruction_renderable.ts:44), so the last label sticks while the final target (and any per-target inner work — replay, sandbox script executions via executeRunOnce) grinds silently; later same-phase stages may emit nothing at all. Fix: finer-grained progress inside the silent stretch — per-target inner-stage labels (e.g. 'reconstructing <target> — replaying run k/n') and/or a heartbeat ('still reconstructing <target>, Ns') so the console visibly advances; audit which Phase-4 stages emit no reportReconstructionProgress at all and give each at least one label. Reproduce with the real ~/.claude/projects RevEng dir (451 targets).
closureNote: Implemented in jfred (staged, uncommitted): every per-target chain stage announces through runStageTolerantly (reconstructing <target> — <stage>) and collectAcceptedUserEditIds labels each branch pass, so the Phase-4 stretch never goes silent; a sync-engine heartbeat is impossible so labels-at-work-boundaries is the fix.

title: Bogus reconstruction targets from Bash command text ('x.taskNumber).join(',')…' reconstructed as a file)
description: During the task-149 stall the progress line read: reconstructing x.taskNumber).join(','))" — i.e. a FRAGMENT OF A BASH COMMAND (a node -e one-liner from a session transcript) became a reconstruction target 'path'. Likely source: discoverScriptCreatedPaths (called in buildRenderableFiles, jfred/src/reconstruction_renderable.ts:36) or the script-run extraction mining paths out of arbitrary Bash command text and admitting garbage tokens as script-created files. On a real messy session this inflates the target list (451 targets for RevEng) and burns reconstruction time on nonsense — possibly the bulk of the 500+ second Phase-4 stall, so fix this BEFORE tuning task-149's progress cosmetics. Fix direction: tighten path candidate validation (must look like a path: no quotes/parens/JS punctuation, plausible separator/extension, or verify existence in evidence channels) at the discovery site, not per caller.
closureNote: Root cause fixed in jfred (staged, uncommitted): bashOverwriteRedirect matched the > inside JS arrows (=>), so parseRedirect minted command-text fragments as redirect targets; a checkCandidateLooksLikePath deny-list at the parseRedirect choke point now rejects non-path candidates.

title: Raw Lines rows: color the line classification distinctly, drop 'Invalid Date', show the { } inspector button
description:
Three fixes for the task-134 Raw Lines rows (kind jsonl-line), scouted 2026-07-21:
1) CLASSIFICATION COLOR: the row text is one string `${verdict.type} · ${verdict.verdict}` (webapp/views/timeline-line-nodes.ts:71) rendered in a single .tl-text span whose class comes from computeRoleClass(kind) — LINE_NODE_KIND falls through to 'role-end' (timeline-render-row-cells.ts:38), so the classification renders in the same color as message text. Split the type/verdict into its own span (or a role pill — computeRolePillLabel in timeline-labels.ts:193 currently returns undefined for line nodes) with a distinct CSS class.
2) INVALID DATE: LineNode.when = verdict.timestamp ?? '' (timeline-line-nodes.ts:68) and the row renderer always prints new Date(node.when).toLocaleString() (timeline-render-rows.ts:110) — empty when → 'Invalid Date'. Two-sided fix: the engine's LineVerdict (src/reconstruction_line_verdicts.ts) should populate timestamp whenever the raw record carries a date field; the renderer should print '' (not Invalid Date) when when is empty/unparseable.
3) MISSING { } BUTTON: checkRowCarriesJsonRecordButton (timeline-sessions.ts:118) returns false when node.uuid === undefined, which covers most raw-line-only records (summary lines etc.), so their JSON can't be inspected. The verdict already knows its 0-based line number (WireLineVerdict.line) but deriveLineNodes drops it — carry `line` onto LineNode, always show { } on jsonl-line rows, and open the inspector by line number instead of uuid.
closureNote: Implemented in jfred (staged): raw-line rows get a distinct role-line classification color, blank timestamps instead of 'Invalid Date' (formatRowTimestamp, also in the details header), and an always-present { } button opening the inspector via the engine's new per-verdict RecordSource file+line (covers uuid-less summary lines; document cache SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 3).

title: 'constructing branches' progress: show an incrementing record counter, not just the static graphic
description: The 'constructing branches' stage shows only the stage label/graphic on the progress bar; the user wants visible forward motion — a counter that increments as records are processed (which record k of N is being handled). Mechanism today: buildProjectReconstruction (jfred/src/viewer_api.ts:65) emits the single stage label PROGRESS_LABEL_CONSTRUCTING_BRANCHES (viewer_api.ts:38, listed in webapp/app-progress.ts:38), then reconstructBranches (jfred/src/reconstruction_engine.ts:212) runs silently: findConversationBranches walks all records, reconstructAll covers the surviving branch (its per-target 'reconstructing <target> n/N' counter exists — task 149 family), and each rewound branch goes through buildRewoundBranchHistory with NO progress emission at all. Fix: thread the existing deep-engine progress channel (reportReconstructionProgress — it already reaches the UI progress line) into the silent parts: a records-walked counter for the branch enumeration ('scanning records k/N') and a per-branch counter for the rewound pass ('rewound branch k of n — <m> records'). Counter granularity: update every ~100 records, not every record — the sink funnels into DOM text and per-record updates would throttle the build it's reporting on.
closureNote: Implemented (staged, not committed): findConversationBranches emits 'scanning branch tips k/N' per abandoned tip and reconstructBranches emits 'reconstructing rewound branch k/N' per rewound branch through reportReconstructionProgress, with 'scanning branch tips' added to the webapp phase-4 classifier.

CANCEL: add a 'Cancel' button ON the progress box that stops reconstruction mid-stream. Abort machinery exists — inflightLoadController (app-fetch.ts:104), already wired to the console's #console-cancel button (index.html:92) and to navigation teardown (app-router.ts:60). Flow: click Cancel -> ask the user to confirm ('cancel this reconstruction?') -> on yes, abort the controller and navigate to the pick-project screen (location.hash = '#/'). Confirm must be an in-DOM dialog, NOT window.confirm — the codebase convention bans native dialogs because they block headless automation (comment at app-header.ts folder-switch handler). Note the navigation to '#/' itself aborts the in-flight load, so 'yes' can simply be: location.hash = '#/' (+ renderRoute if already on #/) — one code path, no separate abort call needed. Also decide whether #console-cancel stays or is retired in favor of the progress-box Cancel (one cancel affordance is enough).
closureNote: Implemented (staged, not committed): the loading overlay is position:absolute inside #timeline-pane so the console stays usable, and the progress box carries a Cancel button with an in-DOM confirm whose 'Yes, cancel' navigates to '#/' (renderRoute aborts the load); #console-cancel retired.

title: Investigate: agent edit near JSONL line 77 has no timeline entry — pre-baseline trim drops the edit's event (baseline-demo)
