title: Phase-4 blowup: nested lineage replays re-run the full per-target pipeline once per (target, timestamp)
description: ROOT CAUSE of the task-156 stall (2252s+ observed on the 451-target RevEng project, 2026-07-21; task 150's garbage-target fix addressed a different symptom). Evidence from jfred-server.log (70s window): 473 'replaying lineage of' headers over only 140 distinct targets — one target replayed 27x, another 56x (sic, from the script-stage tally); plans/items29-30-31-32-close.md replayed 3x in 47s. Mechanism: replayLineageContentBefore (src/reconstruction_branches.ts:199) replays a target's ENTIRE reconstruction pipeline once per (target, before-timestamp) cycleKey, and each replay re-runs every stage including injectScriptExecutions over ALL 1447 discovered runs ('script stage: 1447 runs for <target>' x473). The lineageSeedsByKey memo only caches replays entered on a CLEAN seeding stack (enteredWithCleanStack, lines 207-225) — nested replays recompute fresh every time and are never cached. Also observed: placeGitCommitEvidence is the slowest per-replay stage (0.16-0.37s each; the logged run's last line sat there). Fix directions to evaluate in planning: (a) safely memoize nested replays (the current guard exists because a nested replay's result can be degraded by outer cycle guards — cache only proven-undegraded results, or key the cache by the active seeding stack); (b) compute a target's full revision list ONCE and slice per `before` — CAUTION: enterLineageReplayWindow(before) sets a time cutoff that changes reconstruction (the s87 time-aware indirection), so slicing is only valid where the cutoff provably doesn't alter the prefix; (c) hoist the 1447-run script-run discovery/filtering out of the per-replay path. Reproduce: load project -Users-matkatmusicllc-Desktop-claude-code-src-RevEng with script consent, pipe server stdout to a log, count 'replaying lineage of' repeats per target.
closureNote: Fixed via direction (a), staged in jfred: new reconstruction_lineage_memo.ts tracks per-frame queried cycleKeys and guard-hit poisoning so nested replays are cached only when proven stack-independent and served only when a fresh compute would take the identical path (window-narrowed replays bypass the cache both ways) — provably zero behavior change; direction (c) was found already done (findScriptExecutionRuns is corpus-cached), direction (b) rejected per the task's own cutoff caution.

title: Multi-source reconstruction: multiple conversation-log folders + multiple file-history folders feeding one file's history (in service of task 83)
description:
The jot codebase's revision history — THE reconstruction this whole tool exists for (task 83) — is scattered across at least four conversation-log sources (the original jot project's folder in ~/.claude/projects, the jot-recovery project's folder, this RevEng project, and one or two other projects whose sessions edited the jot plugin from other cwds) and at least two file-history snapshot locations (some under jot-recovery, some under the original jot project's .claude location). Today one reconstruction takes ONE projects folder + ONE file-history dir. Three parts, in this order:
(1) FILE IDENTITY ACROSS SOURCES (investigate FIRST — parts 2 and 3 are only as correct as this answer): how to establish that records/snapshots from different sources refer to the SAME file when sessions ran under different roots (~/Programming/jot vs ~/Programming/jot-recovery vs other cwds) — absolute paths won't match; identity likely = root-relative path agreement (the task-137 repo-matching rule) + content agreement; decide how each source declares its root (per-source cwd remap config, extending the s87 cwd-remap mechanism).
(2) MULTI-SOURCE INPUTS: engine accepts multiple conversation-log folders and multiple file-history snapshot folders for a single reconstruction. Existing seams to extend, not a rewrite: buildProjectReconstruction already merges a LIST of JSONL paths (jfred/src/viewer_api.ts:56 — today all from one folder); snapshots already arrive via the injectable BackupReader (file-history sidecar is a second input; cross-session @vN blob reads already resolve to the OWNING session); config shape probably reveng-paths.json growing source lists.
(3) MERGED PER-FILE RECONSTRUCTION: define how one file's revision timeline is built when its events come from several session logs and snapshots from several folders — cross-source interleaving by timestamp (wall-clock skew between machines/sessions?), what wins when sources disagree, and how branch/rewind structure from different logs composes.
(4) NEW SCENARIO REQUIRED: create a new scenario that covers what is being built — a multi-source capture (run via /run-scenario like the sNN suite) where MULTIPLE files are edited across MULTIPLE sessions run from different project roots, producing multiple conversation-log folders and multiple file-history snapshot folders, with ground-truth revision ladders spanning the sources (cross-source interleaves and root-relative identity matches across differing absolute paths). Coverage bar: exercise essentially everything scenario s87 exercises — the newer-CC wire format and its four mechanisms (cwd remap, time-aware indirection, result-instant rename stamping, git-INDEX staged-blob evidence) — just split up across the multiple sessions. The scenario joins the executed sweep and becomes the acceptance gate for parts 1-3.
(4a) RUN-SCENARIO TOOLING PREREQUISITE: today /run-scenario (jfredToolsPlugin:run-scenario) executes each scenario in a random temp directory — a multi-session scenario needs the ability to SPECIFY where the modifications happen (named/fixed workspace roots reused across the scenario's sessions), so add that capability to the run-scenario skill + scripts first.
Scope note: this is engine-architecture work — plan it (design doc first) before touching code; the 87-scenario sweep must stay green since single-source is the degenerate case.

title: CLI mode: bounded reconstruction up to a file's FIRST revision
description: User request (2026-07-23, during task-182 attempt 2): a mode where I can specify the first commit beacon to start from (--base-commit), provide a bunch of JSONLs and File History Snapshot paths, and a file name, and tell the engine to give me the first revision of that file — reconstructing everything up until that first revision and STOPPING there. Today no flag does this: --step <N> exists but renderStep/reconstructStepStates computes ALL step states for the whole transcript first and then slices out step N (no early stop), and --file/--target filters at RENDER time after full reconstruction (task 181). Natural lever: the strictly-before replay-window machinery (enterLineageReplayWindow / selectRunsWithinReplayWindow) already bounds work by an instant — a CLI flag (e.g. --until-first-revision <file>, composing with --file/--json) could locate the target's first event instant and bound the entire reconstruction at it. Side benefit: on the task-182 real-data set, plate_cli.py's first revision sits early in session time, so the bounded window would keep the script-run pool tiny and sidestep most of the task-192 re-execution blowup — this mode may let 182's 9d14d60d blob check run even before 192 is fixed. EXTENSION (user, same conversation): the bound should be the END OF THE AGENT TURN containing the chosen revision, not the raw revision instant — the file may be revised several times before that turn ends. Generalized contract: "<file> was revised <N> times across [set of JSONLs]. Find the end of the turn for the nth revision of <file> and reconstruct ALL files up until the end of that turn." So the flag takes an optional revision ordinal (default 1 = first), locates that revision's containing turn, resolves the turn's end instant, and bounds the whole reconstruction there; the output should also report the target's total revision count so the user can pick n on the next invocation.
closureNote: Implemented --until-revision <path> [--nth <n>]: locates the nth revision via extractFileEvents, truncates the merged record stream at the containing turn end (next genuine main-chain user prompt) before the sidecar reader/engine run, and reports the total revision count on stderr; work staged in jfred, not committed.

title: executeRunOnce re-execution blowup on real data: one run sandbox-executed ~12,000 times
description: Task-182 attempt 2 (2026-07-23, run KILLED after ~1.5h with ladder.json still empty) hit a task-162-class blowup one layer down: the sandbox-execution memo does not hold across passes. Evidence (log preserved at ~/Programming/jot-recovery/run-evidence/plate_cli_progress-attempt2-2026-07-23.log.gz, plain-text tail alongside): `executing script run` appeared 12,101 times but only 122 distinct run timestamps — the single run at 684c147c-375f-449f-8e32-3847c8cb94ab.jsonl:605 (2026-04-25T01:50:53.814Z, a compound chmod+bash of skills/todo/tests/hook-mktemp-pending-test.sh) accounts for 11,980 executions; every other run executed once. Target discovery stalled (distinct lineage targets 42/156/165 across log quarters while executing-lines went 64/6006/6031). Mechanism to investigate: executeRunOnce memoizes on `timestamp|code` but the cache lives in getDerivedCaches(records, reader), keyed by records-ARRAY identity — per-branch passes (selectBranchRecords, collectAcceptedUserEditIds) and lineage replays hand the engine fresh filtered arrays, each getting a fresh executionsByRun, so runForTarget/runTouchesTarget execution probes re-run the same script per (target x window x records-identity). Fix direction: make the execution memo survive records-identity churn (e.g. key the corpus caches on the underlying session set, or hoist executionsByRun to a run-identity-keyed store like the task-162 lineage memo), WITHOUT breaking the s85 range-patch semantics (see tasks172-173 memory: s85 CI failure was task-155 semantics, not machine-boundness). Blocks task 182 (S9 real-data viability rerun).
closureNote: Fixed by the target-scoped surviving fast path + Bash-executor sandbox skip gate (jfred@cdeef5b); user ran the real bounded plate_cli.py benchmark 2026-07-24 and reconstruction was very fast.

title: CLI flag to decline pre-baseline reconstruction (the iterative loop needs the window cut)
description: Task-188 finding (2026-07-25): the iterative reconstruct -> commit -> re-seed loop cannot actually start from the new hash, because preBaselineReconstructionAllowed defaults to true and ONLY the viewer flips it (src/reconstruction_base_commit.ts:33 — "the CLI never touches it"). computeSkippedBaselineCutoff therefore returns undefined on every CLI run, so a later --base-commit does not prune the records before it: the re-seeded run measured 48s vs the control 49s and its ladder still started ~11 hours before its own seed instant. Add the CLI equivalent of the viewer's "No" to the pre-baseline question (e.g. --no-pre-baseline) so a re-seeded iteration reconstructs only forward from the seed, then re-measure the loop with it. Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 188 — the iterative reconstruct -> commit -> re-seed loop".
closureNote: Implemented --no-pre-baseline in reconstruction_cli_args.ts (parseArgs + applyCliPathOverrides -> setPreBaselineReconstructionAllowed, set unconditionally so an in-process run never inherits a previous answer); 2 new tests green. Re-measured on real data: the mid-window re-seeded ladder went 20 -> 10 revisions, 66s -> 39s, and now starts exactly at its own seed instant (2026-05-14T03:06:21Z), so the loop finally cuts the window.

title: Mid-stream base-commit seed yields a non-monotonic ladder with a duplicated snapshot revision
description: Task-188 finding (2026-07-25): seeding --base-commit at a commit INSIDE the recorded window (step 4 of the iterative loop) corrupts the emitted ladder for common/scripts/plate/plate_cli.py. The gitBase: overwrite lands at index 10 stamped 2026-05-14T03:06:21Z, before an index-11 revision stamped 2026-05-13T21:45:19Z (non-monotonic), and snapshot 04b5333dde2392bd@v2 appears TWICE (indices 8 and 11) where the same-bound control run against the original baseline emits it once — 20 revisions vs the control 18, entirely accounted for by those two artifacts. Both the control and iteration-1 ladders are monotonic, so the trigger is the mid-window seed placement (see reconstruction_git_placement.ts / seedBaseCommitBeacon in reconstruction_base_commit.ts). Fix the ordering + dedupe, or refuse a mid-window baseline with a clear error. May be resolved by task 223 (dropping pre-seed records) — verify before assuming. Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 188 — the iterative reconstruct -> commit -> re-seed loop".
closureNote: Reproduced with four captured runs before fixing. The duplicated-snapshot half was already resolved by task 223 (--no-pre-baseline removes both the @v2 and @v1 duplications). The surviving non-monotonicity was localised by probe instrumentation to seedStaleEditBases pushing a backup-sourced seed stamped with the backup own instant, clamped only against the following edit and never against the preceding event. Fixed with clampSeedBetweenPreviousAndEdit in reconstruction_sidecar.ts giving the seed a two-sided window [previousEventTime, editTime); seedBeforeEdit deleted. 14 tests green; real-data verification passed 10/10 checks with exactly one timestamp re-stamped per run, no revisions added/dropped, no changeId churn, and final content byte-identical to the control.

title: Layer 1: capped-gap ruler axis (instants to pixel offsets)

This preserves ordering and short-gap proportionality while keeping a months-long history on one screen. NOTE it accumulates — position i depends on every earlier gap — which is exactly why it cannot live in CSS the way S8's --axis-ms does; resolve once, globally, and hand the page finished pixel offsets. Ruler bounds fall out of the same ordered set: start = the earliest instant (which a disk orphan predating the first commit legitimately moves earlier), end = the newest disk mtime. Unit test: a 5-hour gap yields 12.5 px, a 6-week gap yields exactly 24 px, ordering is preserved, and a pre-first-commit disk orphan becomes position 0. Spec: specs/from-scratch-SPEC.md S18; mockup: plans/layer1-mockup.html; reuse as much existing engine code as possible (Key Decisions)

title: Layer 1: pair by relative path, classify the two orphan sets
description: S18. Join the task-230 `current file state` against the task-231 `starting repository state` on exact relative path (same name AND same path relative to each list's own root). Emit three results: the PAIRS (each becomes a file widget), the repo-only paths (the "No on-disk match" bucket) and the disk-only paths (the "No repository match" bucket). Buckets are omitted when empty. OUTPUT SHAPE (user-settled 2026-07-25) — the engine emits JSON with exactly these three property names, and they are the names the webapp renders: `pairs` (paths present in BOTH), `gitOrphans` (paths in the repo with NO on-disk counterpart — the "No on-disk match" widget), `diskOrphans` (paths on disk with NO repo entry — the "No repository match" widget). Do not rename or invert these: the two orphan sets read as mirror images and a swap is invisible to the task-238 acceptance test, which only counts two buckets either way. REQUIRED TEST (user-requested 2026-07-25): assert the emitted JSON's `pairs` / `gitOrphans` / `diskOrphans` contain exactly the expected PATHS — this test is strictly about what gets extracted, matched and orphaned. title: Layer 1 View: explain (or fix) commit hashes rendered directly below a timeline bubble

Closed together with the second round of #247 (user re-reported the collision via specs/bug screenshots/on-disk collision inside bubble.png): #248 and #249 were two descriptions of ONE cause in buildPairWidget (jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts), which anchored on pair.commits[0].axisPx unconditionally and hardcoded --span-px to the on-disk node, so a file whose disk mtime predated its first commit produced a negative offset and, because nodes are abspos under translate(-50%,-50%), drew the disk node above the lane top while the lane was simultaneously too short when the last node was a commit; now startPx = Math.min(...nodePx) and --span-px = Math.max(...nodePx) - startPx over every node offset, which also retires the old empty-ladder fallback. title: Layer 1 View: add a minimap of the whole render showing the current viewport
description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-25, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). Add a minimap of the entire render so it is easy to see where in the timeline view the user is currently looking. PLACEMENT: the minimap lives in the LOWER-LEFT CORNER of the timeline pane (user, 2026-07-25) — it must be pinned to the viewport corner, not to the scrolling canvas, so it stays put while the canvas scrolls under it. Motivation: the scroll bars only appear while the view is actively being scrolled, so at rest there is no indication of position within a render that is far larger than the viewport in both axes. The minimap should show the full extent of the canvas and a movable/indicative viewport rectangle, and should stay correct under the zoom control added in task 242 (jfred/webapp/layer1-zoom.ts, native CSS `zoom` on `.canvas`). Design reference: plans/layer1-mockup.html renders it as a `.minimap` block absolutely positioned in a non-scrolling wrapper around the scroll container, with one scaled rect per widget plus a `.mm-view` viewport rect driven by scrollLeft/scrollTop, and click-to-scroll.
closureNote: Implemented as jfred/webapp/layer1-minimap.ts pinned in a new non-scrolling .stagewrap around the scroll container, with one scaled rect per widget and a .mm-view viewport rect plus click-to-scroll. Zoom correctness came from measuring rather than deriving: the module never reads --zoom at all, because native CSS zoom participates in layout so scrollWidth/scrollLeft/getBoundingClientRect already report zoomed values, and .timelines sits OUTSIDE the zoomed .canvas so both live in one coordinate space and mix with no correction factor. Redraw is a ResizeObserver on .canvas, guarded by an observedCanvas check because re-observing an already-watched target re-fires immediately and would loop forever from inside a draw; listeners are re-registered per draw via named function references (a duplicate addEventListener is a spec no-op) so no wired flag can drift. 4 new tests in jfred/tests/layer1-minimap.test.ts stub per-element layout because happy-dom has none. FOLLOW-UP (jfred@f27922c, same session): the user reported the vertical scaling was wrong — fitMinimapScale returned ONE uniform min() scale applied to both axes, so on the ~156,000 px-wide canvas the width term dominated and every mark collapsed into the top fifth of the plot. Each axis now scales to its own extent. The original test fixture could not have caught this: 1000x500 into a 100x50 plot makes both ratios exactly 0.1, and a fixture whose axes agree cannot distinguish a per-axis scale from a uniform one; it is now 1000x250 (x=0.1, y=0.2) and a uniform scale fails four assertions.

title: Layer 1 View: size ruler spacing from measured bubble height instead of a fixed gap
description: Layer 1 View layout fix (2026-07-25, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). The contents of bubbles get squished because the ruler spacing is fixed: every ruler entry is allotted the same vertical gap regardless of how much a bubble needs to show. Evidence: specs/bug screenshots/'squashed bubble contents colliding.png' — a bubble whose file name, commit hash and 'on disk' rows are all crushed into two overprinted lines. Build a mechanism that computes how tall a bubble needs to be in order to show everything it contains (file name, all commit nodes, all on-disk nodes), and use that computed height to drive the spacing of each ruler entry rather than the current fixed pitch. Note the S18 feedback batch already added a ruler gap FLOOR and CAP (jfred/src/layer1_ruler_axis.ts) — this task replaces the floor heuristic with a real content measurement. Depends on the collision fixes so the measurement reflects the final bubble layout.
closureNote: Replaced the guessed 16 px gap floor with a real content measurement: layOutNodeLadders in jfred/src/layer1_ruler_axis.ts takes every bubble's node ladder and charges each instant's gap for the rows hanging below it, gap = max(min(max(linear,16),120), rows(earlier) x 22). Row demand is PER-LADDER, not global — bubbles sit side by side, so two files committed in the same second cost nothing and only two nodes inside ONE bubble must stack. RULER_NODE_ROW_PIXELS = 22 is derived, not chosen: a 15 px .node dot in a 2.5 px ring is 20 px outer, which is where two rows stop touching, plus a 2 px hairline, matching ROW_PX in the signed-off plans/layer1-mockup.html. Content outranks the cap, because a capped gap would clip back the rows it was just charged for. The endpoint folds each node's row into its shipped axisPx so webapp/layer1-page.ts was NOT touched and the page still does no arithmetic. resolveInstantOffsets was deliberately left byte-identical because src/viewer_api_layered.ts (task 239) still calls it. Fixture expectations moved only where a sub-floor gap existed: SECOND_COMMIT_PX 136 to 142, SHARED_FILE_PX 152 to 164, DISK_ONLY_FILE_PX 202 to 214, while the 20-hour gap stayed at exactly 50 px as the load-bearing negative check that content never shortens a gap that already has room.

title: Layer 1 View: add jump buttons for the 'No Repository Match' and 'No disk match' buckets
description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-25, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). Add a button that jumps the view to the 'No Repository Match' bucket, and a second button that jumps the view to the 'No disk match' bucket. Both buckets already exist in the render; these are navigation shortcuts so the user does not have to scroll the full canvas to reach them. They must land correctly under the zoom control (jfred/webapp/layer1-zoom.ts).
closureNote: New jfred/webapp/layer1-jump-buckets.ts wires two header buttons that find the .filebox.bucket whose .fname matches and call native scrollIntoView({block:'center'}). The bucket title is not duplicated as a TS literal — each button carries it in data-bucket next to its visible label, so one literal per direction lives in the markup. Lookup runs on CLICK, never at wire time, because buckets do not exist until the ~10 s stream resolves and every Load replaces them. An absent bucket is matched by heading rather than by index (S18 drops an empty bucket entirely, so 'the second bucket' is unreliable) and degrades to a silent no-op via optional chaining, with a test asserting the surviving button still works afterwards. .jumpbar takes flex-basis:100% so it wraps to its own header row rather than unpinning .layerbar from the right edge.

title: Re-center the clicked node in the timeline area that survives after the inspector opens
description: User request 2026-07-25, in their own wording: "when the inspector is displayed, the clicked node should center itself in the displayed timeline area (an area which shrank because the detail view was shown)". Opening the inspector reveals/grows the details pane, which reflows the split and SHRINKS the timeline pane, so the row the user just clicked can end up off-screen or under the pane edge — the click's own target is what they lose sight of. Centering must run against the POST-reflow layout, never the pre-open one. PRIMARY SITE (jfred/webapp): `openNodeInspector` in webapp/views/timeline-render-inspectors.ts:179 — the opener shared by the `{ }` row buttons and DetailsContext.openNodeInspector — calls through to `openInspectorPane` (webapp/inspector.ts:64), which calls `revealDetailsPane()` and thereby shrinks the timeline, but performs NO scroll afterwards. Note its existing comment: it "deliberately does NOT re-call selectTimelineRow ... reopening the selection would loop" — so the fix is a bare re-center of the already-selected row, NOT a selectTimelineRow call, or the loop that comment guards against comes back. Two places already get this right and are the pattern to copy: `selectTimelineRow` (webapp/views/timeline-render-selection.ts:33) ends with `row.scrollIntoView({ block: "center" })` AFTER awaiting the details render ("item 50"), and the `/at/<n>` deep-link path (webapp/views/timeline.ts:246) opens the inspector and only THEN center-scrolls ("item 37 ordering"). SECOND SURFACE: the same rule applies to the Layer 1 Detail View drawer in task 257, which shrinks the timeline HORIZONTALLY rather than vertically — there the clicked node must center in the remaining left half, so the scroll is on the inline axis, not the block axis. Confirm with the user whether 258 covers both surfaces or only the existing webapp before implementing.
closureNote: Fixed at the shared funnel rather than the reported symptom site: openNodeInspector's four branches (openToolCallLine, openSessionEndTranscript, openLineRowInspector, openTurnInspector) and the /at/<n> deep link ALL route through openTranscriptInspectorSynced, so one line there — context.selectedRow?.scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) — covers every opener instead of four patched call sites. webapp/inspector.ts was deliberately NOT touched: openInspectorPane also runs on every Prev/Next showLine, where syncSelectedRowToShownLine's deliberate block:'nearest' must win, and centering there would yank the timeline on every in-inspector step. The loop the existing comment guards against cannot return because nothing re-enters selection; post-reflow measurement is guaranteed because revealDetailsPane runs synchronously before the call returns and scrollIntoView itself forces a layout flush. 2 new tests pin both invariants: a selectTimelineRow spy that must stay at 0 calls, and a stub recording that #inspector had already lost .hidden at scroll time.

title: Layer 1 View: clicking a ruler row centers that instant's bubble in the visible timeline area
description: User feature request 2026-07-25, in their own wording: "Click on a ruler row and the timeline bubble scrolls into the center of the visible timeline area." The ruler is the sticky left gutter in jfred/webapp/layer1.html; its rows are the per-instant ticks jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts renders from the `ruler` array the /api/layer1-view endpoint returns (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts). Today a tick is inert text — this makes it a navigation control. TARGET RULE, settled with the user 2026-07-25 when asked how to resolve a tick that several bubbles share: center the bubble that BEGINS at that instant (its first node is that tick), and — the user's words — "if no bubble starts there, scroll to the node at that timestamp". So the lookup is two-stage: (1) a pair widget whose first node sits on the clicked instant wins; (2) failing that, fall back to any node placed at that instant and center the bubble containing it. Center means the visible timeline area, so it must be measured AFTER any pane that shrinks the view has settled — see task 258, which is the same centering-against-post-reflow-layout requirement for the inspector, and task 257's Detail View drawer, which takes the right half. Must also stay correct under the zoom control (jfred/webapp/layer1-zoom.ts applies native CSS `zoom` to `.canvas`, so raw offsetTop/offsetLeft values are in unzoomed units while scrollTop/scrollLeft are not — the earlier zoom work already hit this class of bug). Give the ruler rows a pointer cursor and a hover state so they read as clickable.
closureNote: New jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-click.ts turns each DRAWN ruler tick into a navigation control (only drawn ticks, since TICK_LABEL_MIN_GAP_PX skips colliding labels). The two-stage lookup the user settled needs no extra wire data or data attributes because a .filebox's own --axis-px IS its startPx: stage 1 is a direct equality against the tick's offset, and stage 2 falls back to bubbleAxisPx + nodeAxisPx since node offsets are widget-relative. Native scrollIntoView({block:'center',inline:'center'}) reads live layout at click time, which is simultaneously the answer to the post-reflow requirement and to CSS zoom. Orphan buckets are legitimate targets since a bucket is placed at its earliest member's instant. The 3 tests use a fixture deliberately built so a one-stage implementation FAILS — the bubble merely holding an interior node on the shared instant is drawn first, so naive document-order matching returns the wrong bubble.

title: Layer 1 View: add a jump-to-bubble text input so a named file can be scrolled to without hunting
description: Layer 1 View debugging affordance (user-directed 2026-07-25). Purpose: the agreed verification workflow is that Claude makes a visual change, names ONE bubble for the user to look at, and the user checks it by eye in their own running viewer — but the live jfred render is 808 widgets across ~156,000 px, so locating a named bubble by hand is the slow step that undermines the whole handoff. MECHANISM: a debugging text input in the layer1.html header. The user types a file name and the timeline viewport scrolls to that bubble. A `?focus=<path>` query parameter was considered and REJECTED by the user 2026-07-25: copying a long URL out of the CLI session's text output is HARDER than typing a value into a text box, so the deep link would not get used. Build the text box only — do not add the query param until something actually consumes it. Claude's side of the handoff is therefore to name a short value the user can TYPE, not a link to copy. REQUIREMENTS: (1) The input must accept what the user can SEE, which since task 245 is the BASENAME only — typing `launch.json` must work without the full `.vscode/launch.json`. (2) Basename collisions are common and must not be an error: this repo alone renders `.claude/launch.json`, `.vscode/launch.json`, `.vscode-parent/launch.json`, `tasks.json`, `.vscode/tasks.json` and `.vscode-parent/tasks.json`. Jump to the first match and provide a next-match affordance (repeat submit / Enter cycles to the next, wrapping) with a `2 of 6` style counter, so an ambiguous basename is navigable rather than rejected. Accepting a full or partial repo-relative path to narrow it is a bonus, not a substitute. (3) Scroll BOTH axes — a bubble is placed vertically by its earliest instant via margin-top and horizontally by its column index in .stage — and CENTRE the bubble in the pane rather than leaving it at an edge. (4) Briefly highlight the landed bubble so it is obvious which one was targeted. (5) Never a silent no-op: an unmatched name reports into the #crumb. (6) Account for the zoom control — offsetTop/offsetLeft inside the zoomed .canvas are unscaled, so verify the scroll lands correctly at a zoom other than 100%. CONSTRAINT: jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts is AT the repo's hard 250-line cap, so this needs its own module (jfred/webapp/layer1-focus.ts) in the same way layer1-zoom.ts and layer1-progress.ts were split out.
closureNote: New jfred/webapp/layer1-find-file.ts adds a Find bubble box to .sources. One case-insensitive substring test against .fname's title (the full path) satisfies both the basename requirement and path narrowing with no second code path, because a basename is a substring of its own path. Collisions are navigable rather than rejected: a changed term lands on match 1 and an unchanged term (repeat Enter) steps forward and wraps, with the crumb reporting '2 of 3 . <full path>' since a bare counter does not say which of six you are on; an unmatched term reports into the crumb and resets cycle state. The landed bubble is flagged with an outline rather than a border, because a border change would move the bubble's own box, which is the exact geometry the page exists to inspect. Deviation from the task text: the module is layer1-find-file.ts, not the suggested layer1-focus.ts. The rejected ?focus= query param was correctly NOT built.

title: Bug: horizontal dashed lines don't extend all the way to the ruler
description: Layer 1 View bug (user report 2026-07-25). The horizontal dashed lines that connect a bubble to its ruler tick do not extend all the way to the ruler, leaving a gap.
closureNote: Root cause was not a short dash: the leader is .filebox::before running leftward and is DELIBERATELY hidden behind the sticky opaque .ruler, so the dash only appears to start at the gutter's edge. The gutter was 96 px wide while its rail sat at left:80px with a 2 px border, leaving 14 px of opaque background painting over the first 14 px of every dash at every scroll position and zoom level. Fixed by making .ruler carry --rail-x:80px and width:calc(var(--rail-x) + 2px) with .ruler .rail reading the same custom property, so the gutter can never again be wider than the thing it draws, and moving the 14 px to .canvas{gap:14px} — the stage still starts at canvas x=96 so no widget, node, tick or axisPx value moved. No test added: two CSS constants with no branch, and happy-dom has no layout engine so an assertion would only restate the stylesheet. ROUND TWO (jfred@f27922c, same session): the round-one gutter-overpaint fix was a real defect but NOT the one reported — the user re-reported the gap, and their screenshot showed dashes on rows with no bubble in sight, i.e. leaders belonging to bubbles scrolled off to the RIGHT, which `width: 100vw` ended a viewport short of the gutter. A flat 500,000 px width fixed it (user CONFIRMED the lines now reach the ruler) but caused the severe performance regression in task #263, and the leader was finally moved off the bubble entirely onto the ruler entry by task #264.

title: Layer 1 View PERFORMANCE REGRESSION: interface extremely slow and laggy after the leader-line fix
description: Layer 1 View performance regression (user report 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's words: "the interface is now extremely slow and laggy". Introduced by the round-two fix for task #262, which changed `.filebox::before` in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css from `width: calc(100vw / var(--zoom,1))` to a flat `width: 500000px`. That is ONE 500,000 px-wide dashed border PER BUBBLE, and the live jfred repo renders 805 bubbles, so the browser is asked to paint an enormous dashed area every frame. Task #264 is the intended ROOT-CAUSE fix (one shared leader per ruler entry instead of one per bubble); this task is to confirm that is really the cause and to verify the interface is responsive again once #264 lands. If it is NOT the cause, profile before changing anything else. Do not simply revert to 100vw: that reintroduces the original #262 bug where leaders from off-screen-right bubbles stop in mid-canvas.
closureNote: CONFIRMED FIXED by the user on a hard reload 2026-07-26: "the page is much more responsive". The cause was as suspected — the round-two fix for #262 had made `.filebox::before` a flat 500,000 px-wide dashed border, and the live jfred repo draws 805 bubbles, so the browser was asked to paint an enormous dashed area every frame. Closed by #264's structural fix (one shared leader per ruler entry) rather than by reverting to 100vw, which would have reinstated the original #262 defect. Regression introduced and fixed within the same session.

title: Layer 1 View: draw at most ONE dashed leader line per ruler entry, shared by every bubble starting at that timestamp
description: Layer 1 View correctness + performance fix (user report 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's own words: "multiple bubbles that have a dashed line connecting to the ruler that all share the same starting timestamp should only result in 1 dashed line that is used by all of them" and "there should be at most one dashed line for every entry in the ruler, regardless of how many timeline bubbles that start at that timestamp". TODAY: the leader is `.filebox::before` in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css, so there is one per BUBBLE (805 on the live jfred repo) and bubbles sharing a start instant each draw their own overlapping copy. WANTED: the line belongs to the RULER ENTRY, not the bubble — draw it once per entry in the `ruler` array that /api/layer1-view returns (rendered by renderRulerTicks in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts) and let every bubble at that instant share it. This is also the root-cause fix for the performance regression in task #263 and probably for the slow minimap scrolling in task #274, since it replaces ~805 enormous painted elements with a few hundred small ones. Note task #265 changes what these lines align to vertically, and task #268 may reduce the number of ruler entries further.
closureNote: The leader line now belongs to the RULER ENTRY rather than to the bubble: renderLeaderLines in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts draws one `.leader` per entry in the wire `ruler` array into a `#leaders` container, and the `.leader` rule in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css spans it `left: 0; right: 0` against `.canvas`. Anchoring to `.canvas` and NOT `.stage` is what lets a line reach the sticky gutter with no length guess at all — `.stage` begins to the right of the ruler, which is why the per-bubble version needed an ever-growing width and ended up at 500,000 px. DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY: a leader is drawn for EVERY ruler entry, including entries whose label renderRulerTicks drops via the 13 px overprint skip, because a skipped label still has bubbles sitting on it and dropping its line would strand them with no connector; leader count and visible-label count are therefore allowed to disagree. New tests in jfred/tests/layer1-page-leaders.test.ts (split from layer1-page.test.ts at the 250-line cap) pin two bubbles on one instant sharing a single line, a leader surviving a skipped label, and zero leaders inside `#stage`.

title: Layer 1 View: align the dashed leader lines with the NODES at the top of a bubble, not with the top of the bubble box
description: Layer 1 View visual fix (user report 2026-07-26, voice). In the user's own words: "the dashed lines should be vertically aligned with the nodes at the top of a timeline bubble, not aligned with the top of the bubble itself. the dashed lines are meant to indicate which timeline ruler row goes with which timeline bubble event." TODAY: `.filebox::before` in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css sits at `top: -2px` of the bubble box, but a bubble's box top is its padding-box, which sits ABOVE its first node — the bubble carries a derived 50 px padding-top for the file name and sub-line (see the padding-top comment in that stylesheet). title: Layer 1 View: group same-timestamp nodes in a bubble behind a visual indicator
description: User request 2026-07-25, in their own wording: "visual indicator of some kind in the timeline bubble when two events happen at the same timestamp. maybe a rounded rectangle is put around the same-time nodes". WHY THIS IS REAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: a commit instant and a file's on-disk mtime routinely land on the SAME instant (a commit written and the working tree touched in the same second), and that tie is the mechanism behind the overprinting in specs/bug screenshots/'colliding filenames, commit nodes overlapping text.png' — `5636d8ec` drawn straight on top of `on disk`. Task 251 makes the tied nodes stop overlapping by giving each one its own row slot and charging the ruler for it, but once they are on separate rows NOTHING tells the reader they were simultaneous — the fix for the collision destroys the information. This task restores it: draw a rounded rectangle (or equivalent grouping affordance) around the run of nodes that share one instant, so the reader can see the rows are one moment rather than a sequence. The single tick that instant occupies on the ruler is the anchor the rectangle should read against. DESIGN REFERENCE: plans/layer1-mockup.html already computes exactly the grouping this needs — each node carries a `slot` index within its instant and `rowsAt` maps an instant to how many rows it needs; a run with `rowsAt > 1` is precisely a same-timestamp group. The fixture's README.md widget has a real tie (commit 4d5e6f70 and its mtime both at 2026-07-20T16:00:00Z), so the mockup can demonstrate the indicator without new test data. Implementation lands in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts plus the layer1.html style block.

title: Layer 1 View: jumping to a bubble does not bring the bubble's TOP into view
description: User report 2026-07-26, in their own wording: "clicking a file in the file nav correctly jumps to the bubble in the timeline but the top of the bubble is not scrolled to; the scrolling appears to be horizontal only", and separately "the find bubble search field and cycling through the search results via the enter key does not scroll the top of the bubble for the selected search result in to view". ONE root cause serves both symptoms. jfred/webapp/layer1-find-file.ts's jumpToNamedBubble calls `landed.scrollIntoView({ block: "center", inline: "center" })`. A `.filebox` is as tall as its own ladder span (jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css: `.filebox` takes `margin-top: calc(var(--axis-px) * 1px)` and `.lane` takes `min-height: calc(var(--span-px) * 1px + 18px)`), so a file with a long commit history is thousands of px tall; centring that box VERTICALLY puts its top far above the viewport, which reads as "only the horizontal scroll worked". Both callers route through this one function — the find-bubble box (task 261) and the File Nav leaf click (task 252) — so the fix belongs in jumpToNamedBubble, not in either caller. Likely fix: `block: "start"` while KEEPING `inline: "center"` (the horizontal centring is correct and is what already works), plus a small `scroll-margin-top` on `.filebox` so the bubble's name/sub header is not flush against the pane's top edge. TRAP: verify against a MANY-COMMIT bubble (jfred/webapp/styles.css has a long ladder), never a short one — on a short bubble the centre and the top are close together and the bug is invisible.
closureNote: Closed: landOnBubble now scrolls with block:start (inline:center kept) and .filebox carries scroll-margin-top: 14px; the identical defect in layer1-ruler-click.ts was fixed at the same time (jfred@d4e4ca3).

title: Layer 1 View: a File Nav click piggybacks on the find-bubble search and cycles instead of targeting that one file
description: User report 2026-07-26, in their own wording: "clicking the root level .gitignore file cycles between every instance of gitignore in the timeline. the mechanism of clicking the file and going to the bubble in the timeline seems to piggyback off of the search functionality because when you click on the file name in the file nav, the 'find filename: n of N' in the page header populates with the name of the file you clicked on in the file nav. clicking that file multiple times increments the 'n' of that search result header." title: Layer 1 View: clicking a ruler tick must highlight the node or bubble it lands on, not just scroll to it
description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-26, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). "Clicking a ruler item should scroll to the item that occurred at that ruler's timestamp, and also highlight that node or bubble." The SCROLL half already exists (task 260, jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-click.ts:79 — makeRulerTickClickable calls findBubbleForAxisPx(...)?.scrollIntoView({block:"start", inline:"center"})); what is missing is the highlight, so on a dense stage the user cannot tell WHICH bubble the tick meant. REUSE the existing highlight rather than writing a second one: jfred/webapp/layer1-find-file.ts already has landOnBubble (scrollIntoView + highlightBubble, which adds the `.found` class for HIGHLIGHT_MS = 1500 and cancels the previous bubble's un-lighting timer so two jumps in quick succession do not switch each other off). Both are module-private today — export landOnBubble and have makeRulerTickClickable call it, so the ruler tick, the typed Find box and the File Nav leaf click can never drift apart in landing behaviour. `.filebox.found` is already styled at jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css:245 (3px outline in var(--sel-edge)), so the bubble case needs no new CSS. NOTE the two-stage lookup in findBubbleForAxisPx (layer1-ruler-click.ts:64): stage 1 finds the bubble that BEGINS at that offset, stage 2 falls back to any bubble holding a NODE at it. When stage 2 is what matched, the user asked for the NODE to be highlighted rather than only its containing bubble — there is no `.node.found` rule yet, so one must be added, and findBubbleForAxisPx must return (or additionally report) the matched node so the caller knows which of the two cases fired. INTERACTS with task 284 (a ruler timestamp shared by MULTIPLE nodes), which changes what a tick click does when more than one file was touched at that instant: land the two together, or build this one as the single-match branch of 284's behaviour.
closureNote: Closed: a ruler-tick click now lights the same element it scrolls. `layer1-find-file.ts`'s highlight became the exported, PERSISTENT, single-element `highlightLandedElement` (the 1.5s fade timer deleted on the user's 2026-07-26 instruction) and `makeRulerTickClickable` calls it. NOT via `landOnBubble` as this task's text asked: that predates task 266 and uses `block: "start"`, which would have regressed 266's `block: "nearest"`.

title: Layer 1 View: the hover-revealed full file name blends into neighbouring bubbles names
description: Layer 1 View fix (user feedback 2026-07-26, follow-up to task 280). Task 280 shipped the in-page hover reveal: `.filebox .fname:hover` in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css lifts `max-width`/`overflow` so the whole path runs past the bubble’s 168px, painted over an opaque `background: var(--surface)` at `z-index: 7`. In the user’s words: "change the text color when showing the full file name so it doesn’t blend in with adjacent bubbles’ file names with the same y coordinate." CAUSE: the revealed name keeps `.filebox .fname`’s `color: var(--c-snap)`, the same colour every OTHER bubble’s name uses, so at one y coordinate a revealed long path reads as a single continuous run of green monospace text mixed with its neighbours’ names and the reader cannot tell where the revealed name ends. FIX DIRECTION: change the text colour (and/or raise the background contrast) inside that one `:hover` rule. The opaque background and the z-index are already in place, so this is a colour change only — no geometry change, and nothing outside `.filebox .fname:hover`. TRAP: the page is theme-aware (jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css redefines every token under `prefers-color-scheme: dark` and `[data-theme="dark"]`), so the new colour must be a token that exists in BOTH sets, not a literal.
closureNote: Closed: `.filebox .fname:hover` now paints `color: var(--c-user)`, the orange the user asked for and a token defined in all three theme blocks, so a revealed long path no longer reads as one continuous green run with the neighbouring bubbles' names; colour only, no geometry change.

title: Layer 1 View: dragging the File Nav resize grip causes massive GUI latency
description: Layer 1 View performance bug (user report 2026-07-26, on the task-279 feature just shipped). In the user’s words: "resizing the file nav results in massive GUI latency (probably because the entire timeline canvas is redrawn, not just the visible timeline area)". WHERE: jfred/webapp/layer1-filenav-resize.ts — every `pointermove` writes `--filenav-w` onto `.stagewrap`, and `.filenav`’s width, `.minimap`’s `left` and `.filenav-grip`’s `left` all read that property. CAUSE (to confirm): `.filenav` is a flex SIBLING of `main.timelines` inside `.stagewrap`, so changing its width reflows the timeline pane — and that pane holds ~800 `.filebox` widgets spanning ~156,000px inside a `zoom`-scaled `.canvas`, so each pointermove forces a layout of the WHOLE canvas rather than the visible area. Candidate fixes to weigh: (a) coalesce the writes to one per frame with requestAnimationFrame, the smallest change; (b) take the timeline pane out of the resize’s layout path so its width is not a function of the pane’s — e.g. a fixed flex-basis on `main.timelines`, or drive the pane’s offset instead of the flex row; (c) commit the width only on `pointerup` and show a lightweight preview line during the drag. Verify the cause before picking — if (a) alone makes it smooth, (b) and (c) are unnecessary. Related: task 192 covers this page’s other bounded-perf work.
closureNote: Closed: the drag no longer relays out the ~156,000px canvas per pointermove. It writes a preview-only `--filenav-drag-w` that only the absolutely-positioned `.filenav-grip` reads, plus a `dragging` class, and commits the shared `--filenav-w` exactly once on pointerup. Candidate (a), rAF coalescing, was rejected (browsers already coalesce pointermove to ~one per frame); the user's suggestion to defer the dashed leader lines needs no separate work because the pane's box never changes mid-drag.

title: Layer 1 View: the dashed leader lines and ruler tick labels sit ~52 px above the nodes they mark
description:
Layer 1 View alignment bug, found independently by two agents on 2026-07-26 while working tasks 270 and 268/275/266, and deliberately NOT fixed then: it moves the vertical alignment of every row on the canvas, which the user should sign off on rather than have changed as a side effect of other work.

MECHANISM. A `.filebox` is positioned by `margin-top: calc(var(--axis-px) * 1px)` (jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css), so its BORDER-BOX top is the bubble's first instant. Its nodes live in `.lane`, the first in-flow child, which starts after the bubble's 2 px border and its 50 px `padding-top`. A node's absolute canvas y is therefore `axisPx + 52`, while `.leader` (`top: calc(var(--axis-px) * 1px)`, positioned against `.canvas`) and `.ruler .tick` (same, against `.ruler`) are both drawn at bare `axisPx`. So the dashed connector and the gutter timestamp both sit ~52 px above the dots they are meant to mark.

The comment on `.leaders` claims task 265 made the line land on the nodes — "a node is placed at axisPx - startPx inside a bubble whose own offset is startPx, so its absolute canvas y is exactly axisPx" — but that derivation omits the border and the header padding, so task 265 did not achieve what it documents. Fix the comment along with the geometry.

The 52 px is not a constant of nature: it is `.filebox`'s border plus its `padding-top`, and that padding is itself DERIVED from `.fname`/`.sub`'s `top` values and font sizes (see the derivation comment on `.filebox`), so any change to the bubble header moves it. Task 270 briefly made it 70 px before being reverted.

DECIDE THE FIX WITH CARE: adding the header offset to BOTH `.leader` and `.ruler .tick` keeps the gutter, the dashed lines and the dots agreeing with each other; moving only one of the two would make the ruler disagree with the leaders. Publishing the offset once as a custom property beats repeating the literal in two rules.

VERIFY AGAINST THE REAL RENDER BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING. This is a reasoned reading of the CSS, not a measured screenshot, and the current alignment has shipped through tasks 250, 262, 264 and 265 without complaint — so confirm the offset is really visible before moving every line on the page.
closureNote: Closed: the 52px offset was confirmed by derivation (`.filebox`'s 2px border plus its derived 50px `padding-top`), published once as `--lane-y` on `.canvas` and added to BOTH `.leader`'s and `.ruler .tick`'s `top` so the gutter, the dashes and the dots agree; the `.leaders` comment that wrongly credited task 265 with this was corrected. The user's follow-up idea also landed as a new `webapp/layer1-leader-hover.ts` that recolours a hovered leader and marks every target inside the visible pane.

title: Layer 1 View: global toggle to place bubbles by author vs committer timestamp
description: User request 2026-07-26, in their own wording: "add a global toggle next to the zoom buttons to place bubbles on the timeline using 'author' timestamps or committer timestamps. the 'CommitTouch' interface (/Users/matkatmusicllc/Desktop/claude code src/RevEng/jfred/src/layered_git_beacons.ts) will need 'authorEpochSeconds: number'. Line 31 'listCommitsTouchingFile' will need an optional arg (authorOrCommitter: boolean) to decide how git should be spawned (line 32) to get the author/committer timestamp." WHY THIS IS REAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: on 2026-07-26 the user saw two commits wrapped by task 259's same-instant rectangle whose git-GUI dates were days apart — specs/bug screenshots/'git commit timestamps computed wrong.png'. Verified against this repo: fc5ad81 and e677bd9 BOTH carry `%ct 1783459471` (2026-07-07T14:24:31-07:00) while their AUTHOR dates are Jul 4 and Jul 5. The commits were rewritten in one rebase/cherry-pick, so committer time collapsed onto one instant and author time did not. Neither reading is wrong — committer time answers 'when did this land in this repo', author time answers 'when was this change written' — so the user wants to choose per view. THE VALUE'S PATH, so the choice can be threaded end to end: (1) jfred/src/layered_git_beacons.ts:31 `listCommitsTouchingFile` is the engine's ONLY git-log reader, spawning `git log <ref> --format=%H %ct -- <path>` at line 32; (2) jfred/src/layered_instants.ts:11 `widenCommitterSecondsToInstant` turns those seconds into a Date; (3) jfred/src/layer1_commit_history.ts:29 `listPairCommitHistory` maps each touch to {hash, instant}; (4) jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts:89 `listPairNodeLadder` builds the ladder, :97 `placePairNodesOnAxis` and :112 `placeInstantOnAxis` place it; (5) jfred/src/layer1_ruler_axis.ts resolves the distinct instants into ruler rows; (6) jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts's buildPairWidget draws the bubble and jfred/webapp/layer1-tie-groups.ts groups the equal instants. TWO DESIGN NOTES FOR THE IMPLEMENTER. (a) ONE `git log --format=%H %ct %at` returns BOTH stamps in a single spawn, so if CommitTouch carries `authorEpochSeconds` AND `committerEpochSeconds`, the optional arg on listCommitsTouchingFile becomes redundant — the CALLER picks the field, and git is not re-run every time the toggle flips (the full build is ~10 s on a real project). Settle that against the arg the user described BEFORE writing either. (b) plans/coding-requirements.md forbids boolean parameters (domain types over primitives, single-condition branching), so if the arg is kept it must be a two-member enum (e.g. CommitTimeSource.author / CommitTimeSource.committer), never a boolean. UI AND PLUMBING: the toggle belongs in the header beside .zoombar in jfred/webapp/layer1.html, as its own sibling group in the style of .layerbar. The choice MUST reach the server, because the instants are computed there — the page's inputs already live in the query string (?dir=&repo=&ref=), so add a fourth param, mirror it in jfred/webapp/layer1-sources.ts's readSourceParams/fillSourceBoxesFromUrl, and read it in jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_route.ts. Flipping the toggle re-loads the view; the existing loadbar already reports that build. Finally, `widenCommitterSecondsToInstant`'s NAME and its `widenedFromSeconds` flag describe committer seconds specifically — both stamps are second-precision so the function itself is reusable, but its comment must stop claiming committer-only.
closureNote: Bubbles can be placed by author or committer timestamp: a two-member CommitTimeSource enum, one git log --format=%H %ct %at spawn carrying both stamps, widenCommitterSecondsToInstant renamed to widenEpochSecondsToInstant, the choice threaded through to the route as ?time= and round-tripped in the URL, and a .timebar toggle in the header beside the zoom buttons per plans/layer1-mockup.html.

title: Layer 1 View: clicking a ruler tick shared by multiple nodes expands to list the files touched at that timestamp
description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-26, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). "If multiple nodes occur at a ruler timestamp, clicking that ruler timestamp should expand and show the names of the files that were touched at that timestamp." Today a tick click is single-destination: jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-click.ts's findBubbleForAxisPx returns the FIRST match of a two-stage lookup — stage 1 the bubble that BEGINS at that offset, stage 2 any bubble holding a node at it — and makeRulerTickClickable (line 74) scrolls to it. When several files were touched at one instant that silently picks one and gives the user no way to see the others, which is the reported gap. WHAT TO BUILD: on a tick whose offset is shared by nodes in more than one bubble, the click expands an inline list of those files' paths rather than jumping. Two facts make the lookup cheap and drift-proof, both already true: a `.tick` carries the ABSOLUTE ruler offset in `--axis-px`, and a `.node`'s absolute offset is its bubble's `--axis-px` plus its own (widget-relative) one — the same arithmetic findBubbleForAxisPx already does, so collect ALL matches instead of the first. Each owning bubble's full path is on its `.fname` element's `title` attribute (its visible text is the basename only, task 245). AXIS_MATCH_EPSILON_PX (1e-6) is the tolerance to reuse — it absorbs float rounding, nothing more. OPEN CHOICES for the implementer: where the expanded list renders (inline under the tick inside the sticky `.ruler` gutter, which is only ~82px wide — `--rail-x` 80px plus the rail's 2px border — versus a popover, for which webapp/views/sidebar-coverage.ts's coverage popover and webapp/app-header.ts's toolbar popovers are the two existing patterns); whether clicking a name in that list then jumps to its bubble (probably yes); and how the list closes. INTERACTS with task 283 (a tick click must also highlight what it lands on): 283 is effectively the SINGLE-match branch of this behaviour, so land the two together or build 283 first and add this as the multi-match branch. Related but different: task 259's tie-group markers already handle two nodes of ONE bubble sharing an instant; this task is about nodes ACROSS bubbles sharing one.
closureNote: A ruler tick shared by more than one event now expands into the files touched at that instant: RulerRow carries every offset the printed row absorbed, new webapp/layer1-tick-files.ts holds the lookup, the .tickfiles widget, the single-open-row state and the Escape close, and .tick.multi marks an expandable row at render time; the mockup's push-down of the rows below the open list was deliberately skipped and is recorded in a ponytail: comment.

title: Layer 1 View: confirmed Git repo gets a branch dropdown, and the Commit/branch textbox becomes a commit-history dropdown
description: Layer 1 View feature (2026-07-26, user feedback on jfred/webapp/layer1.html). In the user's words: "the 'git repo' text editor: when a repo is loaded, after the presence of that repo is confirmed, show a 'branch:' dropdown menu with all branch names that let the user pick the branch to use. The 'commit/branch' textbox should be replaced with a dropdown menu showing commit history. The commit dropdown menu should have a width of 75 characters (for the commit message preview) + the timestamp, so the user can see most of the commit message." TODAY: jfred/webapp/layer1.html:41-45 has `<input id="repo" type="text" size="34">` with an "Open…" picker button, and `<label>Commit / branch <input id="ref" type="text" size="10" placeholder="default branch"></label>`. Both are plain text, read by webapp/layer1-sources.ts (SOURCE_PARAM_IDS = ["dir", "repo", "ref"]) and mirrored into the URL as ?dir=&repo=&ref=, which is spec S18's "one shareable link" — so whatever the pickers become, they must still round-trip through those same query params, and fillSourceBoxesFromUrl must still be able to seed them from a link. WHAT IS NEEDED: (1) A repo-EXISTS check, which nothing does today — the current failure mode is that /api/layer1-view returns a 400 whose body message lands in the #crumb (layer1-page.ts's loadLayer1View catch). The dropdowns must appear only after the path is confirmed to be a git repo, so this needs either a new lightweight endpoint or an extension of an existing one. (2) A NEW SERVER ROUTE listing the repo's branches and its commit history — no such route exists (the page's only endpoints are /api/layer1-view, /api/pick-folder, plus /api/config and /api/projects from the classic app). The commit rows need hash, subject and committer timestamp; src/layer1_commit_history.ts and src/layered_git_beacons.ts's listCommitsTouchingFile are the existing git-log readers to model it on, and src/layered_instants.ts's widenCommitterSecondsToInstant is how committer seconds become an Instant everywhere else. (3) The branch dropdown replaces nothing — it is new UI beside the repo box. The commit dropdown REPLACES `#ref`. WIDTH: the commit dropdown is specified as 75 characters of commit-message preview plus the timestamp, so the subject must be truncated to 75 chars server- or client-side and the control sized in `ch` units, not px. OPEN QUESTIONS the implementer should settle with the user: whether picking a branch immediately reloads the view or only refills the commit list; whether the commit list is the branch's full history or a capped head window (a large repo's full log is thousands of rows in a <select>); and whether typing a raw ref must still be possible for a hash that is not in the list — the current box accepts any ref, and a dropdown alone would remove that. NOTE the ~10 s cost of /api/layer1-view (one `git log` per tracked path): the branch/commit listing must be its own fast route, never a side effect of the view build.
closureNote: A confirmed git repo gets Branch and Commit dropdowns: the new fast route /api/layer1-refs returns branches, HEAD and a capped 200-commit head window separate from the ~10s view build; .sources split into a project-folder row and a repository row, the dropdowns stay hidden until the repo is confirmed, the commit list is sized at 100ch, a branch pick reloads the view and a commit pick writes into the surviving #ref box so a raw hash is still typeable.

title: Layer 1 View: mockup session for how a bubble top, its first node and the ruler timestamp should align
description:
Layer 1 View DESIGN-OPTIONS exercise (user feedback 2026-07-26, after task 290 aligned the dashed leader lines and ruler ticks with the NODES via `--lane-y: 52px` on `.canvas`, added to both `.leader` and `.ruler .tick` in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css). In the user’s words: "is the vertical alignment of the top of a bubble and the first commit in the bubble supposed to not line up with the actual timestamp they go with? for example, the git modules file is time stamped at July 16th 19 hours 24 minutes 47 seconds 0 microseconds. the commit hash 082468f2 is in line with that timestamp but the top of the bubble is a few rows above that, to accommodate the text shown at the top of the bubble so that the commit hash remains in line with the ruler time stamp. dialing in the way I want the bubble and first node alignment with the ruler visuals to look should be reserved for a mock-up session so I can see the various options."

THIS IS NOT A BUG FIX. No webapp code changes until the user picks an option.

WHAT TO PRODUCE: a static mockup page — house pattern is jfred/plans/layer1-mockup.html (itself preceded by plans/mvp-app-mockup.html, and the file layer1-styles.css was lifted verbatim from) — rendering the SAME small set of bubbles several ways, side by side or switchable, so the user can compare by eye.

THE GEOMETRY TO VARY: a `.filebox` is placed by `margin-top: calc(var(--axis-px) * 1px)`, so its BORDER-BOX top is its first instant, while its nodes live in `.lane`, which starts after the bubble’s 2px border and its 50px `padding-top`. A node’s absolute canvas y is therefore `axisPx + 52`, and that 52px is exactly what `--lane-y` now adds to the ruler ticks and the leader lines.

OPTIONS WORTH DRAWING: (1) today — ruler and dashes on the nodes, bubble box top 52px above its own first instant; (2) pull the bubble up so its FIRST NODE sits at the box top, header text floating above the box; (3) keep the header inside the box but offset the box so its top edge lands on the instant and the first node sits 52px below, ruler following the node; (4) header text moved out of the box entirely (above it, or into a hover reveal) so the box top and the first node coincide. For EACH option show what happens to the leader line, to the gutter tick, and to two bubbles whose instants are close enough that a 52px shift makes them collide.

TRAP: the 50px `padding-top` is DERIVED, not chosen — it comes from `.fname`/`.sub`’s `top` values and font sizes (see the derivation comment on `.filebox`), and task 270 briefly made it 70px before being reverted, so any option that changes the header changes the number.
closureNote: Closed by the user after reviewing the mockup: the current styling and positioning of bubbles is fine and looks good, so no alignment option needs to be chosen or ported.

title: Layer 1 View: draw the 'created at' on-disk node the mockup has always shown
description: Layer 1 View feature, USER-CONFIRMED 2026-07-27 in the FULL shape (the mockup's rules in full, not a minimal node). The user asked whether each file's created-at timestamp was being COMBINED with its first commit; it is not — created-at is simply UNBUILT. jfred/src/layer1_disk_walk.ts's DiskFileState carries ONLY `mtime` (line 23) and its header comment states the reason: "birthtime is not portable, so it is never read" (spec S18). So jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts's listPairNodeLadder emits commits plus ONE on-disk instant, and jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts's buildPairWidget draws a single `.node.n-disk` labelled "on disk". WHAT THE MOCKUP SPECIFIES (plans/layer1-mockup.html, the signed-off reference): its DISK fixture (line 618) gives every file BOTH `born` and `at`; the widget builder (line 743) pushes a `created at` node ONLY when `disk.born !== disk.at` (lines 748-749 — classes `n-disk n-created`, text "created at", kind "created"), then always pushes the `on disk` node, then sorts the whole node list by instant and assigns tied nodes successive row slots (line 755); `.n-created` is `border-style: dotted; border-color: var(--muted)` (line 316); the legend carries its own swatch `border:3px dotted var(--muted)` labelled "created at" (line 518); and task 257's drawer rule (lines 955-971) makes the created node INERT — `const hot = node.kind !== "created"` — with the non-clickable label carrying `title="created-at is not the latest on-disk state — nothing to show"`, so only the LATEST disk node opens the drawer, and when born === modified the single node IS the latest and IS clickable. THE WORK, END TO END. (1) jfred/src/layer1_disk_walk.ts: DiskFileState gains a birth instant; both statSync call sites (lines 112 and 154) already hold the Stats object, so `stats.birthtime` costs nothing. DECIDE AND DOCUMENT the unreliable-birthtime rule — on macOS/APFS birthtime is real, on ext4 it is frequently 0 or a copy of mtime, so a birth that is epoch-0, later than mtime, or equal to mtime must yield NO created node rather than a false one. (2) jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts: listPairNodeLadder must emit the created instant in the right ladder position (its order is LOAD-BEARING — placePairNodesOnAxis reads the offsets back POSITIONALLY, and the mockup sorts the node list by instant before assigning slots), and Layer1WirePair needs the new node on the wire. (3) jfred/webapp/layer1-wire.ts and jfred/webapp/layer1-filter.ts: the wire mirror and listWirePairLadder must match the server EXACTLY, or a folder filter's client-side re-layout will disagree with the shipped offsets. (4) jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts's buildPairWidget draws it with class `n-disk n-created`; jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css gains the `.n-created` rule; jfred/webapp/layer1.html's legend gains the swatch. (5) jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts must REFUSE the created node unless it is the only disk node, mirroring the mockup's `hot` rule, and set the explanatory title on the inert label — today it treats every `.node.n-disk` as clickable. TRAPS: layer1-page.ts is AT the 250-line cap and viewer_api_layer1.ts is near it, so new behaviour goes in NEW modules; task 259's tie-group markers read instants off the ladder, so an extra node changes which nodes group; and the ruler's per-instant row demand (countRowsPerInstant in jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts) is measured from the ladders, so adding a node per pair changes ruler spacing and every offset after it — the existing placement tests' hand-derived ladders will have to be redone. Also update spec S18, whose disk-walk section currently states that birthtime is never read.
closureNote: Built end to end and user-verified: birthtime read behind readCreatedInstant (rejects epoch-0 and any birth at or after the mtime) plus readPairCreatedInstant in viewer_api_layer1.ts (rejects a birth later than the file's first commit, the checkout time every clone reports), which keeps a surviving created node the earliest in its bubble; shipped on the wire as Layer1WirePair.created and mirrored in layer1-wire.ts/layer1-filter.ts, drawn as `n-disk n-created` by layer1-widgets.ts, dotted and non-clickable in layer1-styles.css, legend swatch in layer1.html, refused by layer1-drawer.ts with the mockup's explanatory title, and spec S18's 'birthtime is never read' replaced with the reliability rule.

title: Layer 1 View: an expanded ruler row's file list overprints the ruler rows below it
description:
User bug report with screenshot, 2026-07-27. Repro: load the Layer 1 View on a real project and click a ruler row shared by several nodes so it expands into its file list (task 284's `.tickfiles`). If the list is long it is drawn straight over the ruler rows beneath it — in the reported screenshot `07-16 21:24:28.15 (28)` is buried under `reconstruction_graph.ts on disk`, and the rows below keep their original y positions.

User's hypothesis, confirmed correct: the y coordinate of every ruler row below the clicked one is not recomputed when the list opens, so nothing accounts for the list's height.

The signed-off design already exists in plans/layer1-mockup.html lines 700-711 and 836-848: `resolveOffsets` takes an `extraAt` map keyed by the LAST instant the expanded row absorbed, carrying the list's height in AXIS pixels (screen px divided by the zoom, because the gutter sits outside the zoom), and the layout runs TWICE — a draft pass to learn which instants the printed row absorbed and how many files those hold, then the real pass with `extraAt` fed in. The mockup deliberately REJECTS drawing the list as an overlay over the canvas: feeding the height into the layout is what makes a bubble spanning the expanded instant GROW instead of being written over.

Implementing it means giving `layOutNodeLadders` in jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts an equivalent extra-height input, and having the expansion in jfred/webapp/layer1-tick-files.ts trigger a full re-layout and re-render rather than only injecting the list into the tick. NOTE: that axis module is shared with the server (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts imports layOutNodeLadders), so the server's own call must keep today's behaviour and every existing placement test must still pass.

Relevant files: jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts, jfred/webapp/layer1-tick-files.ts, jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts (renderRulerTicks / renderLayer1Stage), jfred/webapp/layer1-filter.ts (relayOutLayer1View), jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts. This is task-284 code and predates the 292/294-297 batch.
closureNote: extraGapPx two-pass re-layout on row expansion per the signed-off mockup; server placement byte-identical. User-verified 2026-07-28. NOTE: this task number was independently reused by a Layer 2 mockup task closed 2026-07-27 on the parallel branch.

title: Decide how duplicate snapshots resolve when multiple File History Snapshot folders are configured
description:
User question 2026-07-27 while testing task 296: "How are duplicates (hash and @vN) handled when using multiple FHS paths?"

VERIFIED CURRENT ANSWER: they are NOT handled, because nothing consumes the list yet. Task 296 shipped the picker that stores multiple file-history folders and task 297 saves them to ~/.jfred-layer1-settings.json and .config/debugConfig.json, but the Layer 1 View reads NO file-history at all (spec S18 — it compares a working tree against a git tree, which is the whole point of the task-238 acceptance test). The list is stored and carried for the layer that will read it: layer 3's file-history snapshot beacons (jfred/src/layered_snapshot_beacons.ts, task 201).

The collision is real and must be decided BEFORE that layer reads more than one folder. A file-history store is <root>/<sessionId>/<blob>, where a blob name looks like `971e94bac3cb2811@v2` — so two configured roots can hold the SAME sessionId and the SAME <hash>@vN with DIFFERENT bytes. The obvious case is one root being a backup or partial copy of the other, which is exactly the ~/Programming/jot-recovery/claude-data/file-history vs ~/.claude/file-history pair this project already works with.

Questions to settle with the user:
1. first-root-wins, last-root-wins, or refuse and report a conflict into the health sink the way task 176 made cross-source contradictions do?
2. is identical-bytes-in-both a silent no-op, or still worth reporting?
3. does the ORDER of the folders in the picker define precedence? If so the list's order is load-bearing and the UI should say so.

Relevant files: jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts (the single-root reader and its ~/.claude/file-history default chain), jfred/src/layered_snapshot_beacons.ts, jfred/src/reconstruction_multi_source_join.ts (the existing precedent for merging several sources), jfred/webapp/layer1-source-paths.ts (where the list lives client-side).
closureNote: First-configured-root-wins resolver with health-sink report on differing bytes, picker hint and spec note; policy decided by the user. NOTE: this task number was independently reused by a Layer 2 mockup task closed 2026-07-27 on the parallel branch.

title: Layer 1 View: a Cancel button while a project is loading
description:
User request 2026-07-27. A Layer 1 build takes ~10 s on a real project and there is currently no way to stop one — picking the wrong folder means waiting it out. Add a Cancel button that is shown ONLY while the loading progress bar is up, and hidden the moment the load finishes, fails, or is cancelled.

Cancelling must actually abort the in-flight request rather than only hiding the bar: GET /api/layer1-view is read as an NDJSON progress stream (jfred/webapp/layer1-progress.ts `readLayer1ViewStream`), so the fetch needs an AbortController the button can trigger, and the reader loop has to treat an abort as a clean stop rather than an error in the crumb. Decide what the stage shows afterwards — the S18 precedent is that loadLayer1View already clears the crumb, the stage and the File Nav before a build starts, so a cancelled load leaves an empty stage and the crumb should say so plainly.

There is prior art for the control in the classic webapp: task 164 added a Cancel-with-confirm on the pane-scoped progress overlay. title: Layer 1 View: show a progress bar during 'resolving the ruler', which currently reports nothing
description:

title: Layer 1 View: the JSONL Nav must show a progress indicator while it builds its list
description:
User report 2026-07-27. Symptom: after the timeline is displayed and the ruler resolved, the JSONLs pane shows the empty-state message "no JSONLs touched this project's files" and then a few seconds later populates with the real list. That message is a LIE during the load — it states a finished result while the work is still running — and it reads as the pane being broken or the project having no transcripts.

Cause: renderLayer1View draws the stage first and then fires loadLayer1Sessions() WITHOUT awaiting it, deliberately, so the session scan does not delay the timeline (jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts). GET /api/layer1-sessions parses every JSONL under the configured source folders — measured at ~4 s over 629 transcripts on the user's real config — and until it answers, jfred/webapp/layer1-sessions.ts holds an empty `sessions` array, so renderSessionPane falls straight to its empty-state row.

Deliverable: while the session list is being fetched and filtered the pane shows a progress indicator, and the empty-state message appears ONLY once the fetch has completed and genuinely produced nothing. Reuse the existing loadbar idiom rather than inventing a second one (jfred/webapp/layer1-progress.ts owns .loadbar / .loadbar-fill / .loadbar-label, styled in layer1-styles.css). The pane is narrow, so either a slim bar or a labelled 'scanning N JSONL folders…' row is acceptable — pick one and say why in the code.

Consider whether the endpoint should stream NDJSON progress the way /api/layer1-view already does (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_route.ts is the server precedent, readLayer1ViewStream in jfred/webapp/layer1-progress.ts the client half): a per-file count turns a 4 s blank into a visibly advancing scan. If that is too much, a plain indeterminate indicator still fixes the reported confusion.

This is the first task filed under the user's standing rule (2026-07-27): anything that takes a while to load shows a progress bar.

Relevant files: jfred/webapp/layer1-sessions.ts (loadLayer1Sessions, renderSessionPane and its .navempty row), jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts (renderLayer1View), jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_sessions.ts (the endpoint), jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css.
