title: Layer 1 View: select two nodes on a bubble's lane to diff those two revisions in the Detail View
description:
User request 2026-07-27 (feature). Select two nodes on one file bubble's timeline and the Detail View shows a diff of those two revisions of the file. Detail View header buttons: [diff side-by-side / diff inline] [full content] [export as patch].

Today clicking ONE node opens the drawer on that node's bytes at that instant (task 257, jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts). This adds a two-node selection within the SAME bubble's lane — commit-to-commit, commit-to-on-disk, or on-disk-to-commit — and shows the diff between them instead of one file's contents.

Open questions for whoever implements:
- How the second node is picked. Shift-click is the selection idiom the File Nav folders and the JSONLs pane already use, so it is the obvious candidate.
- How the pair is shown on the lane. A single clicked node already gets highlightLandedElement's marks, and two selected nodes must read as a PAIR with a direction (older = base, newer = target).
- A selection spanning two DIFFERENT bubbles is out of scope: refuse it visibly rather than silently diffing unrelated files.

The three header buttons go in the drawer's header row — the same place task 299 puts the image zoom controls. Do not add a second control strip.

REUSE rather than reimplement. The classic webapp already has the whole diff surface: jfred/webapp/views/details-diff.ts renders side-by-side and inline (renderDiffVsBase / renderRevisionDiff); the server has GET /api/diff (handleDiffRequest in jfred/src/viewer_server_routes.ts, jfred/src/viewer_api_diffs.ts) and GET /api/range-patch (handleRangePatchRequest, jfred/src/render_git_diff.ts), which is what 'export as patch' wants.

BUT note the constraint that shaped this drawer: the Layer 1 page deliberately imports NOTHING from webapp/views/, because that drags app-routes.ts → inspector.ts → timeline-*.ts — the entire classic app — into a page that loads only layer1-*.js (see the header comment of jfred/webapp/layer1-file-view.ts). Decide up front whether to lift the diff renderer into a shared module both pages import, or to copy it the way task 257.4 copied the numbered-row renderer.

A new server route is likely needed regardless: /api/diff is keyed by project/target/revision numbers out of a reconstruction document, whereas Layer 1 identifies its two sides by (repo, hash, path) and (dir, path) — the same inputs GET /api/layer1-file already takes — so the natural shape is a layer1 diff route taking two such sides.

Relevant files: jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts, jfred/webapp/layer1-file-view.ts, jfred/webapp/layer1-widgets.ts (the lane and its nodes), jfred/webapp/layer1-find-file.ts (highlightLandedElement), jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_file.ts, jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css.

Related: task 299 (image viewer, same header row) and task 218 (segment patch emitted as git-diff), which already specifies patch emission for a different selection model and should be read before designing 'export as patch'.

title: Layer 1 View: a bubble's node does not line up with the ruler timestamp its hover leader line points at
description:
USER-REPORTED 2026-07-27 with a screenshot (file snapshot name `971e94bac3cb2811@v2`, two adjacent bubbles both showing the truncated name `971e94bac3cb2811…`). Mousing over the bubble or one of its nodes draws the dashed green leader line horizontally from the node across to the ruler gutter, but the ruler tick label the line arrives at is NOT the node's own timestamp. In the screenshot the left bubble's `on disk` node and the right bubble's `created at` node both sit roughly 260 px BELOW the `07-20 19:19:03.46 (30)` tick and about 175 px ABOVE the `07-20 19:19:03.47 (14)` tick, so the leader lands in empty gutter between two labels and the reader cannot tell which instant the node belongs to.

WHAT TO WORK OUT: which of the three y-sources is wrong.
(a) `jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts` — `accumulateOffsets` charges the gap LEAVING an instant `countRowsPerInstant(instant) * RULER_NODE_ROW_PIXELS`, and that per-instant row demand is a MAX taken across EVERY ladder, so an instant at which one bubble stacks many nodes opens a tall band that every OTHER bubble's single node at that instant sits at the very top of. The ~440 px between two ticks only 10 ms apart is exactly that band, which makes this the leading suspect.
(b) `jfred/webapp/layer1-widgets.ts` — `buildPairWidget` offsets the whole `.filebox` to `startPx = min(node axisPx)` and then draws each node at `axisPx - startPx`, so any error in the box's own anchor shifts every node inside it together.
(c) the leader line itself (`jfred/webapp/layer1-page-leaders.ts`, with the tick rows in `jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-rows.ts`) — it may be drawn at the NODE's y while a tick label is drawn at its instant's row-0 offset, in which case the line is honest and the LABEL placement is what is off.

RELEVANT PRIOR DECISION, do not silently reverse it: spec S18 records that a ruler tick sits a fixed 52 px above the first node of its bubble (the `.filebox` border plus its top padding) and that the user ACCEPTED that inset on 2026-07-25, with the bubble's TOP EDGE — not its first node — being the thing that lines up with the tick, matching to within 1.5 px for all 807 widgets. The gap in this screenshot is far larger than 52 px, so this is a DIFFERENT defect, but any fix must preserve that accepted top-edge correspondence.

The report arrived immediately after task 298 added a per-pair `created at` node, which changes each pair's ladder and therefore every ruler offset after it. Check whether the defect predates 298 by loading the same view at the commit before jfred@90cd007.

SECOND SCREENSHOT (same session, ruler row expanded and the Detail View open, so paths are readable). The clicked node is `971e94bac3cb2811@v2`, whose Detail View header reads `demo-corrupt/file-history/2c6a7ebe-c18b-472a-829d-46902eb5ff7e/971e94bac3cb2811@v2 · working tree` — so every bubble in this cluster is a FILE-HISTORY SNAPSHOT file inside the demo-corrupt bundle, not project source. Expanding the `07-20 19:19:03.46 (30)` tick lists its 30 events, and three things in that list matter:
1. The SAME path appears MANY times over, e.g. `971e94bac3cb2811@v2 on disk` on several separate rows. Those are separate bubbles for one path — the duplicate-file-history-path case that is known to be unhandled. Whether one path legitimately produces several pairs is part of this bug, because each duplicate contributes its own node at the instant.
2. Both KINDS appear at this one instant for one path: `971e94bac3cb2811@v2 on disk` and `971e94bac3cb2811@v2 created at`. A created node is only emitted when the birth is strictly EARLIER than the mtime, so those must be two DISTINCT instants that the gutter's centisecond-rounded label prints identically. Confirm whether the label's precision is hiding separate ticks — if so, two visually identical labels can sit hundreds of pixels apart and the leader line will look wrong even when it is correct.
3. The expanded list overprints the ruler rows below it (already filed as its own task) — do not re-fix that here, but it makes reading this screenshot harder and the two defects may share the row-height arithmetic.

REPRO: the demo-corrupt bundle's file-history folder, the cluster around 07-20 19:19:03.4x.
closureNote: Diagnosis proved the geometry honest — centisecond labels merged distinct millisecond instants; fixed with millisecond ruler labels per the user's choice. NOTE: this task number was independently reused by a Layer 2 mockup task closed 2026-07-27 on the parallel branch.

title: Layer 2 engine: snapshot discovery per owning session for the Layer 1 View route
description:
Spec S19; the signed-off mockup is plans/layer2-mockup/ (index.html + fixture.js + app.js, 43 headless checks in jfred/scripts/visual/mockup.ts via `npm run visual:mockup`). Layer 2 is the SNAPSHOT layer — the JSONL layer was dropped, not deferred (second renumbering pass in the spec's Key Decisions).

The engine core already exists and must be REUSED, not rewritten: jfred/src/layered_snapshot_beacons.ts's collectSnapshotBeaconNodes (task 201, spec S4) already walks buildBackupTimeline(records, findCwd(records)) and resolves every non-null backupFileName through a per-OWNING-SESSION BackupReader — which is the whole point, because `abc123@v2` recurs across sessions with DIFFERENT bytes. What does NOT exist is a path from that to the Layer 1 View route: jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts reads NO JSONL at all by design (S18), so Layer 2 is the item that introduces JSONL and file-history as inputs to that route.

THE WORK: new jfred/src/layer1_snapshots.ts exporting a function that takes the JSONL session file paths and the file-history root(s) and returns, per ABSOLUTE file path, a list of SnapshotPlacement { path, version, instant, sessionId, sessionFile, line, backupFileName } ordered by instant. Reuse what is there: parse each transcript with jfred/src/parse/loadTranscript.ts, build the reader with buildSidecarReader(records, sources) or createSidecarReader(sessionId, root) from jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts, and take the points from buildBackupTimeline (BackupPoint = { backupTime, backupFileName | null, sessionId }). `version` is the `@vN` suffix parsed off backupFileName and is numbered PER SESSION — never treat it as a global identity; the mockup fixture deliberately carries src/util.ts @v2 from b21d84c5 AND a different @v2 from d4a06b8f for exactly this reason. Version 1 carries a null backupFileName (no blob) and is SKIPPED, the same rule collectSnapshotBeaconNodes already applies. `line` is the transcript line the backup point was recorded at — task 311 needs it to pick the customTitle in effect.

Do NOT read blob bytes here. The wire carries PLACEMENTS only and the bytes are fetched on demand by task 313: a project with hundreds of snapshots would otherwise pay a full read on every view build, which already runs ~10 s.

Root discovery: resolveFileHistoryRoot(records), deriveSiblingFileHistoryRoot(projectsDir) and deriveFileHistoryRootFromRecords already exist in jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts — an explicitly-supplied root WINS and discovery is the fallback (the S1 rule).

VERIFY: unit test with two fixture sessions using the same `@vN` name for different bytes — each placement carries its own sessionId, and reading through each session's reader yields that session's bytes. Second test: a null-backupFileName v1 produces no placement. TRAP: the file-history reader falls back to the LIVE ~/.claude/file-history when a test does not load through loadTranscript, so a careless test silently reads the developer's real machine and passes for the wrong reason.
closureNote: Implemented as jfred/src/layer1_snapshots.ts (collectSnapshotPlacements; BackupPoint widened with version/line) with unit tests; full suite green and user verified.

title: Layer 2 engine: JSONL session metadata and the customTitle in effect at a line
description:
Spec S19, "JSONL Nav row order" and "Snapshot node click". Two consumers need this. The JSONL Nav row is three parts — truncated `<filename>.jsonl`, then the session's customTitle values deduped (omitted when it has none), then `<start timestamp> · N files`. The snapshot drawer header reads `<filename> Snapshot - <customTitle>`, where that title is the one IN EFFECT OVER THE LINE RANGE WHERE THE SNAPSHOT OCCURRED, not the session's first or last. A user may rename a session more than once, so a session's title is a FUNCTION OF POSITION in the file; picking the wrong one attributes a snapshot to work it has nothing to do with. The mockup fixture carries session b21d84c5 with two titles over two line ranges and a snapshot inside each, precisely so a grab-the-first or grab-the-last implementation is visibly wrong.

THE WORK: new jfred/src/layer1_sessions.ts exporting (a) a builder returning, per session file, { file, sessionId, started, ended, paths[], titles: [{ fromLine, title }] } and (b) a pure `titleInEffectAtLine(titles, line)` returning the last title whose fromLine <= line, or undefined when the session was not yet named at that point. The record already parses: RecordType.customTitle = "custom-title" in jfred/src/structures/vocabulary.ts, the title rides on the record's `n` key, and jfred/src/reconstruction_json.ts already walks them. `started` and `ended` are the session's FIRST and LAST record instants — deliberately NOT the instants of the files it touched, because the Nav band has to be able to open before the first write and close after the last one (the mockup fixture states this rule explicitly). `paths` is what the session wrote, which is all task 292's filter needs; the timeline those paths draw still comes from the repo and the disk, so a file keeps its whole history even when the session touched it once.

VERIFY: unit tests — a session with two titles returns the FIRST for a line inside range one and the SECOND for a line inside range two; a line before the first custom-title record returns undefined; an unnamed session yields an empty titles list. Deduping is a DISPLAY concern that belongs to the Nav row, so the builder returns every range rather than a deduped set — the drawer needs the ranges the Nav throws away.
closureNote: Implemented as jfred/src/layer1_sessions.ts (buildSessionMetadata + titleInEffectAtLine) with unit tests; full suite green and user verified.

title: Layer 2 engine: snapshot nodes on the Layer 1 wire, ruler and shared axis
description:
Spec S19. Extend jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts's Layer1WireView so every pair — and every DISK ORPHAN, since a file can be snapshotted without being in the repo — carries `snapshots: Layer1WireSnapshot[]`, where Layer1WireSnapshot extends Layer1WireInstant with { version, sessionFile, sessionId, line }. The route gains `?jsonl=` and `?snapshots=` params for the session and file-history roots (task 310's inputs) and round-trips them through the URL exactly as ?dir=&repo=&ref=&time= already do, so a Layer 2 view stays one shareable link; tasks 295 and 296's pickers write into these same params.

The payload ALWAYS carries snapshots regardless of the selected layer. The layer switcher is a client-side show/hide (task 314), and refetching on toggle would pay the ~10 s build twice.

Snapshot instants are REAL ruler entries: they join the capped-gap ladder, they get ticks, and they count toward Layer1WireRulerTick.eventCount. So they must flow through layOutNodeLadders in jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts — the module the server and the client SHARE — not be bolted on afterwards. Per the S19 CORRECTION of 2026-07-27, a pre-commit snapshot does NOT pull a bubble's anchor earlier: `born <= snapshot <= mtime` is physics and `born` is itself a node, so no snapshot can ever be a bubble's earliest node; what it does instead is take a ruler entry above every commit, which lengthens the ladder below it. Add a progress label for the new stage beside the existing LAYER1_PROGRESS_LABEL_* constants — the snapshot read is new cost in a build that already runs ~10 s, and this project's standing rule is that anything slow shows progress.
